evidence: "Observations were canceled today due to the celebration of the end of an era of Rubin Construction." "Observations canceled for the night. Tour demonstrations were given, no problems." Planned (event), not weather/fault. No weather summary.

"Simonyi's first night of operations! All tests run according to plan." Venting 23:30 UTC, prepare-for-on-sky 00:00 UTC, initial alignment BLOCK-T539, stability test, FBS survey BLOCK-T624; "We closed the dome at 7:50 UTC" (DomeAz failed on close, recovered). Daytime faults only (Chiller 1 reset, dome current issue, CalSys). Weather: "cloudy in the last couple of hours … transparency decreased". Mirror cover failed to close twice (OBS-1154). Close at 07:50 UTC is ~1.5 h before twilight but the report gives no reason — slight ambiguity, hence low non-zero P.

"We completed all scheduled Simonyi tests, though we encountered some issues during the run." Louver E1 22:30 UTC, shutters 23:00 UTC; initial alignment converged to 0.4″; "MTRotator FAULT (OBS-902, 20 min lost)"; "MTAOS faulted due to MTRotator not reporting angle (OBS-1304, 48 minutes lost)"; thermal degradation, M1M3TS setpoints adjusted ~04:10 UTC; "We closed the dome at 8:25 UTC". ≈1.1 h lost to faults. Weather: thin clouds, winds 4–9 m/s, no loss stated. AuxTel not operated (ATMCS faults, OBS-1294).

"Unfortunately for Simonyi we lost almost the entire night due to a series of major faults that reduced total on sky time to about 30 - 45 minutes." Dome shutter fault during handover 19:38→23:25 UTC ("~3.5 hours"); "Shortly after getting on sky, dynalene chiller 01 failed and we had to swtich, causing a 3-hour delay for camera"; network crash (IT pixel-firewall work) "lost most AT and MT systems"; "M1M3 faulted … 45 minutes of recovery"; "We closed early and ran dynamic tests instead." Weather: wind dropped to ~3 m/s at open, no weather loss.

Dome shutter and louver opened 23:34 UTC; "Simonyi was on-sky at ~ 00:10." "Shortly after getting on sky, the camera team alerted us to a dynalene emergency. They had to power off all CCDs and REBs. Recovery took several hours, but we determined that getting back on sky was a risk with the camera in an unsecured state. We spent the remainder of the night doing calibration and CBP testing. (OBS-1310)". "Weather cooperated all night." Daytime: GIS interlocks, M1M3/M2 faults, LOVE lost 2.5 h, MTRotator pull-cord (OBS-875).

"The night was dedicated to AOS testing." Shutter and louver opened 23:14 UTC; initial alignment then LUT-005; "multiple CSCs failed (MTMount, MTRotator, and MTPtg), triggered by the CCW — please refer to OBS-738 … Approximately 20 minutes were lost." "We ran out of time for the last elevation 25." Cryo 6 trip at end of night killed the daily cals only. Weather: "clear skies throughout", wind ~5 m/s. ≈20 min lost to fault.

"Lost majority of tonight due to humidity, and clouds". "We opened dome and louver at 23:18 UTC (humidity ~ 60 %) … humidity reached eventually to 80 % so quickly, so we closed the dome immediately at 23:44 UTC. The dome never go reopened due to fluctuating humidity, continuous drop in ambient outside temperature … and later dense cloud coverage." "First 3 hrs after sunset were humid (>65% relative humidity) and later half of the night was completley overcast". Closed-dome time: TMA dynamic tests, whitelight flats, CBP QE sweeps (tunable laser power-off issue OBS-1230, random rotator fault — no sky loss). "We went on sky for last 1.5 hrs" with bad seeing; initial alignment and focus sweeps. AuxTel also shut down for humidity > 80% (AuxTel statement).

"initial alignment at 00:16 UTC and completed at 01:09:48 UTC"; "MTAOS went into fault at 02:43 UTC … repeatedly (three times) and also repeated failures of the track target and take image scripts … we lost approximately three hours of observing time. Observations resumed at 05:40 UTC." Weather clear, wind 14 m/s (AuxTel shut down 02:19 UTC for wind — AuxTel statement). ≈3 h lost.

"Smooth night with AOS verification at the start … and FBS … for the remainder of the night." Vent 23:04 UTC, initial alignment 00:00 UTC. Winds 10–15 m/s later; "30 min Observing time loss in between due to winds" is in the AuxTel section (AuxTel statement).

"Relatively smooth night operation, only one dome failure. Cloudy weather during the night, and seeing not good." "Starting at ~4:10UTC we got scattered moonlight from clouds … switch to FBS with bad seeing (T630)"; "At 7:30UTC the sky turned clear." Dome motion fault (OBS-646) "recovered quickly". Dome stayed open; cloud-degraded rather than lost — ambiguous, mid probabilities.

"Smooth day and night for both Simonyi and Auxtel." MTRotator fault (OBS-922) recovered by cycling; Scheduler 1 fault (OBS-1341) re-enabled. FBS "for over two hours before closing the dome at 5:20 CLT". No time loss stated.

Power glitch: "We started the morning with a power glitch at the observatory. It caused dynalene, TMA IS, GIS, and M2 CSC issues." "around 20:40 UTC we were unable to turn on the power supply for the TMA … GIS interlock on the OSS"; "given control of the TMA at 23:50 UTC … skip directly to opening the dome". Second power glitch: "Around 02:25 UTC we experienced an M1M3TS failure … right after a three-phase power glitch; Petr recovered the system at 02:58 UTC" (≈0.5 h). Closed dome 08:10 UTC. Night otherwise "smooth overall".

Planned: "No scheduled on-sky operations for Simonyi today." "Today is a closed dome day for Simonyi" (mirror cleaning, UPS work); "Smooth calibration night" (CBP, monochromatic flats until 09:30 UTC). Weather would also not have allowed opening: "humidity jumped to 100% … clouds covered the entire sky … −2°C … A little bit of snow floating in the air"; AuxTel "bad weather prevented us from starting venting or on-sky" (AuxTel statement).

"at 22:38 UTC, we got M1M3, M1M3TS, and MTMount Fault while just waiting for sunset … OSS fault at ~23:01 UTC (OBS-1352) … OSS took 45 minutes to power back on, we were just in time and we started initial alignment ~ 21:25 UTC" (time as written; likely 23:25). During the night: MTRotator fault (OBS-992), EAS fault (OBS-1353), MTPtg rotator motion lock — no durations given. "Night time operations was good overall, minor issues encountered." Finished scheduler 08:10 UTC. Small unquantified fault interruptions.

"MTMount, MTPtg, and MTRotator repeatedly entered FAULT states … azimuth encoder heads … overall time loss over 1 hour." "Near the end of the night, OSS failed (OBS-1267, 1 h lost) and humidity reached 66%, so we decided to stop FBS survey and close the dome shutters and louvers". ≈2 h fault; humidity contributed to the early close near end of night (hours not given).

"Night operations run smootly for Simonyi, good image quality and one fault that took no time fix." "Scheduler:1 went to STANDBY state by itself … (OBS-1362, ~5 min lost)." Venting delayed to 23:50 UTC by "high external temperatures" (not a loss). Dome closed 08:10 UTC.

Opened 22:49 UTC. "during the second TMA pointing, we had an OSS fault (OBS-1364), which caused a 2.5-hour downtime." Then "seeing worsened, so we stopped the test" and ran ~30 min FBS. Closed 08:10 UTC. ≈2.5 h lost.

"started the initial alignment at 0:13 UTC and had a rough start … we stopped receiving Data from Rapid Analysis … .nan in the FITS Seeing Header (OBS-1366) … insufficient Quota (OBS-1367) … At 3:30 UTC we were finally able to start with the AOS tests (Timeloss of 2-2.5h). The rest of the night went flawless". Clear, sub-arcsec seeing. ≈2–2.5 h lost.

Dome open for vent 22:51 UTC. "AOS testing run all night, and TMA was a total peach. However, upon closing, we had issues with M2Hexapod and with M1M3. These errors blocked us from taking the cals" (OBS-1375) — after dome closure, no on-sky loss.
"Quiet calm night of AOS testing. No faults." Shutter opened at sun −4°.

"Simonyi took 3 hours of ToO data!" "We experienced a brief dome error, but we continued the rest of the night smoothly." "Mild winds and photometric conditions all night long." M1M3 fault during calibrations (after close).
"went on sky at 00:25 UTC"; ToO, T641, T640, T559, T614 run through the night; no night-time loss stated. Script failure OBS-1382 was during daytime checkout.

"Smooth nighttime operations with no Simonyi or AuxTel faults except for minor dome issues." Opened for venting 22:34 UTC; "exposures 34-71, there is some vignetting because we lost the dome following."

"on-sky with both telescopes at −5 deg sun elevation". "We got an MTDome error for azimuth, but it was solved very fast. The FES error was harder to solve because the permissions are not in place for the OS team (45 min lost)." ≈0.75 h lost. Mid-layer clouds in the afternoon; FWHM 0.8–1.4″ stable all night.

"On-sky observations with Simonyi were delayed by ~2 hours due to a problem with the cryo 6." "Cryo 6 failed at Nov 19, 0:34 UTC due to a PLC communication loss … the OSS was turned off and the dome was closed … PLC auto-recovered at ~1:08, and Cryo 6 was back online by 1:23." ≈2 h lost; then ToO, T559, T645.
"The night continue without incident; the only problem was the M2 hexapod, which for some reason CSC fault when moving the TMA (OBS-1400)." Running on Mitsubishi generator (planned, no loss stated).

"Disaster night, TMA debugging for 4.5 hours followed by a camera issue. No on-sky data except for initial alignment." Power glitch: "Around 15.05 we moved facility power from generator to commercial grid … a glitch of about 30 seconds that affected mainly the dynalene system flow" (FRACAS-321); wavefront sensor HV off was "a residual issue from the power glitch". Alignment done 01:25 UTC; TMA fault, "brought back at 06:10AM UTC (time loss 4.5h)"; then camera focal plane stuck; "close dome ~20m early". "Quiet night, low wind, humidity ~30%."

Opened 00:00 UTC, alignment 00:27, ToO from 01:12 UTC. "TMA Drives issue (OBS-1401) and OSS fault (OBS-1267) at the same time at 02:17 UTC. Recovery took 25 minutes … resume the ToO at 02:48 UTC"; "camera focal-plane issue at 04:02 UTC (LSSTCAM-148, time loss ~ 20 mins)". T513 2.75 h, T614 from 07:28, closed 08:01 UTC. ≈0.75 h lost. Clouds forecast but no weather loss reported.

"Troublesome night, camera faulted three times (jgroup storm), 1h time loss." Alignment 00:20 UTC; LSSTCAM-148 recovered in 5 min; "We met twice camera faults, first one being recovered quickly but second one took ~1 hour (OBS-1336)"; "closed the dome ~5m early". "Clear skies overnight." ≈1 h lost.

Power glitch: "one power glitch event sent everything south. Almost every system went to FAULT and took altogether 6.5 hours for full recovery." Dome opened 00:02 UTC; "a commercial power glitch caused a commercial power outage at the summit"; OSS/PS, Dynalene, HVAC, M1M3, rotator, hexapod, CalSys, ESS, TMA PILZ/EtherCAT faults; closed-loop issue "lost almost 2 more hours" (OBS-1406). "Finally, after 6.5 hours of troubleshooting we were able to complete the initial alignment and start the FBS observations which took ~ 30 minutes." "Perfect night conditions, clear skies, no wind, low humidity." ≈6.5 h lost.

"Almost every system was pretty stable during the night." Opened 23:48 UTC, alignment 00:23 UTC, Chaos Monkey 01:41–03:15 UTC (two MTAOS, MTPtg, MTRotator faults "recovered by recycling"), T641, T635, FBS from 07:22, shutdown 09:22 UTC.

"during venting at 23:09 UTC, the Dynalene flow rate dropped to zero (OBS-1416) … the camera had to be powered off". "Start-of-night was delayed slightly by the camera recovery, followed by a longer delay due to the initial alignment not working due to some configuration mismatch (OBS-1415)." MTQueue misbehaviour, rotator/AOS faults interrupted blocks; FBS standard config failed (OBS-1420). "Night work was productive, completing all planned tests, despite numerous faults." Hours lost not stated — delay length ambiguous. Clear skies.

Louvers 22:38, shutters 22:58 UTC; alignment at sun −10°, IQ ~0.8″. "Night operations were again productive despite some faults" (HV trip on one sensor OBS-1423, abandoned T540, rotator offsets OBS-999, script-config failures OBS-1414/1426). "Stopped the FBS at astronomical twilight." GIS communication loss (OBS-1427, ~45 min) was after dome closure — calibrations abandoned, no on-sky loss.

Power glitch: "There was a commercial power outage that lasted 10min (Mitsubishi generator turned on) … we were delayed from on-sky observations due to TMA and dome issues (OBS-1401 and OBS-1428; 1.5hrs lost)." Then pre-LSST survey all night. "After a couple of MTDome faults followed by a cascade of CSC faults from a possible GIS connection issue (OBS-1428 and OBS-1427), we ended the night early (~1 hour of time loss)." "The sky was clear throughout the entire night." ≈2.5 h lost.

"Around 6:00 UTC, MTScheduler CSC crashed, losing heartbeats, and went into Standby … (OBS-1431; time loss ~0.75hr)." MTAOS issue flagged images (OBS-1430). Closed ~08:00 UTC. Daytime "brief power cut that only impacted the second-level lights" (power glitch, no impact). Humidity jumped 20→40–50% "causing alarm over the dew-point difference with the cryo 1 hex temperature but no greater concerns". ≈0.75 h lost.

"Flawless night in Simonyi and AuxTel. About 490 LSSTCam science images non-stop taken by the Scheduler." Dome opened fully at sun −5° (20:50 CLT) after atypical temperature oscillation during venting.

"We lost the TMA's encoders multiple times, which caused the elevation and azimuth axes to fail. Most of the night was focused in TMA recovery and troubleshooting"; "azimuth dirty encoder tape … (4h lost)". "In the last third of the night we performed an AOS stability test on a fixed position." "Clear skies … winds below 5 m/s." ≈4 h lost.

Clear. "Nighttime observations were conducted in a restricted range of azimuth that seemed to avoid the TMA encoder errors" (OBS-965). "difficulty with the correct_pointing script (OBS-1434) which extended the alignment time somewhat"; Chaos Monkey "waiting nearly an hour between perturbations instead of the desired 30 minutes". "AOS and FBS filled the night". Minor loss only.

Clear, warm night. "Initial alignment, pointing correction and start of the AOS tests went well… The night ended with FBS-driven observations until astronomical twilight." Encoder issue resolved in the afternoon; "cleared to run the TMA at the full range of azimuths tonight".

"Smooth day and night filter offset testing. We only missed the last LUT version due to time constraints." Two problems "quickly resolved": MTCamera CSC fault from network traffic (OBS-1441), CCW limit switch alarms (OBS-875). Minor loss.

"At 6:30 UTC temperatures dropped by 2C over ~10 minutes and humidity spiked to 78%." "interrupted by an MTMount azimuth encoder fault (OBS-1445), and then by a chorus of humidity alarms which forced the dome closed more than an hour earlier than planned. We did not finish the v7 LUT and no FBS observations were done." Closed-dome stray light (CBP) afterwards.

"Full cloud cover during the night." "We try to go on sky, we don't get any star (8hrs lost for on-sky observing) so we just run all night BLOCK-T563 LSSTCam PTC Curve". Dome was opened at sunset but no on-sky data; treated as a weather closure. AuxTel statement: "8hrs lost" to weather too.

"We could not vent before sunset as there were heavy clouds and virga present." "we struggled to get in good focus the telescope the entire night, we barely finish the Block 559, only with r>>i filter." "big drop in temperature from 9 to 8 degrees in just 5 minutes. After that the OSS went to fault. and we lost 45 minutes of sky time." (≈ 0.75 h; OSS fault triggered by the temperature drop — mixed).

"It rained and hailed today! Due to risk of water falling into the dome upon opening the shutter, we took the decision to keep MT closed tonight." Rain/hail 21:45–22:45 UTC; "at 06:00 UTC… still water dripping from the building". In-dome tests and calibration; FCS troubleshooting ~1.5 h (OBS-1448) and FiberSpectrograph Kafka error (OBS-1449) during the closed night. AuxTel statement: opened after inspection.

"clear skies and smooth operations… minimal observing time loss (~20min total due to faults, 0hr due to weather)". "The TMA azimuth axis faulted in the middle of the night (OBS-958 and OBS-959), losing ~20min of observing time." Cryo trim heat <10 W at ~6:45 UTC but "approved to continue".

Clear. Dome venting 0:10 UTC, initial alignment 0:40 UTC. Camera trim heat sank to 2.23 W, "urged us to lower the TMA to 32 deg to recover the Cryo". "At 7:44 UTC the Rotator got too old Telemetry from the CCW and failed which we took as a proper reason to close for the night". "Overall it was a good night". Earthquake 6:41 UTC, no failure. Minor loss.

Clear. "Venting was delayed due to warm temperatures outside the dome. We opened at a Sun elevation of –6°, and the first alignment was performed at –12°." "ran all night using the Hexapods with the V22 LUT". "Near the end of the night, an MTRotator fault triggered an MTPtg fault. Both were recovered". Daytime OSS fault recovered ~3 h later (before night). Minor loss.

"Although rain and thunder were predicted, the night was exceptionally clear with low humidity". Venting 23:15 UTC, initial alignment 0:36 UTC, closed 8:30 UTC ("first on-sky observations until the beginning of nautical twilight"). "MTRotator getting old Telemetry from the CCW (OBS-922) which delayed the tests a bit." Daytime Dynalene alerts during glycol switchover. Minor loss.

"Clear night with good seeing. Observations interrupted for >1 hour due to an FES fault". Opened 23:15 UTC, alignment finished 1:10 UTC; "MTCamera faulted because of an FES error reported in OBS-1454… solve the issue after 1.3h. At 4:20 UTC, we were back on sky"; closed 08:36 UTC. (≈ 1.3 h lost.) Daytime OSS/MTMount fault (OBS-1453) recovered before night.

Mixed. "An unrecoverable problem with the OSS stemming from Chiller 2 prevented us from observing with Simonyi, either on sky or in closed dome." "High humidity prevented us from observing until 05:40 UTC" ("thick clouds… humidity raised above 70%"). Electronics team: "TMA was not safe to use during the night"; only i-band whitelight flats. Weather would have closed until ~05:40 UTC; the fault removed the rest.

"big and thick clouds came from the South and the humidity rose up to 82%. The humidity reached to >90% at 23:00 UTC"; "around 01:00 UTC it had decreased enough for on-sky observing. Simonyi observed with the FBS for the remainder of the night". "EAS frequently faulting and a CCW error, but minimal time was lost." Chiller 2 back online 13:00 UTC.
"Simonyi performed well all night. BLOCK-559 observations took all night" (~6.5 h). "sub-optimal IQ due to the TS not quite meeting the warmer temperatures", M1M3TS operated disabled. Warm, clear.

"Around 23:30 UTC, many CSCs went into fault due to an unknown GIS reboot (details in OBS-1474, ~3hrs of time loss)… re-enabled OCPS.101… (OBS-1101, 0.3hrs time loss)—we were on-sky around 2:40UTC." FBS 4:25–8:02 UTC. Daytime: OSS fault (OBS-1473), dynalene lost 21:42 UTC, camera recovered 00:00 UTC. (≈ 3.3 h lost.)

"Excellent sky conditions… New record in image quality… 0.58 FWHM." Alignment 00:47 UTC; BLOCK-T667 2:58–8:35 UTC, "delayed due to a CCW fault recovery and TMA drive issues (OBS-1478, ~1.5hr time loss total)". Daytime dynalene loss 14:23 local, recovered 14:59 (OBS-1476).

Clear. "Observations tonight were littered with many faults from various subsystems." Dome open 00:26 UTC; "Delay to get on-sky due to azimuth encoder issues (OBS-965, 0.37 hours time loss)"; during T559 "issues with the MTRotator (OBS-1481), M1M3TS (OBS-1344), TMA drives (OBS-641), and MTDome azimuth drives (OBS-646). Total time loss was ~1.4hrs." FBS 7:30–8:39 UTC. (≈ 1.8 h lost.)

"lost 2 hours Simonyi (1 due to weather and 1 due to M1M3TS in FAULT)". Dome opened 23:42 UTC; "Dome closed at ~4:00 UTC due to humidity reaching over 75%… we re-open at 4:55 UTC (~1h lost to weather)"; "M1M3TS in FAULT (OBS-1344, ~1h lost)". Dome closed 8:47 UTC. Unstable seeing.

"Smooth Simonyi operations but with poor seeing throughout the entire night, peaking at ~3.3″." Dome opened 00:08 UTC, closed 08:40 UTC. Wind up to ~15 m/s; M1M3TS in degraded mode. No lost time stated; seeing-limited block choice only. AuxTel statement: closed for wind gusts at 4:34 UTC, "loosing the last 4 hours".

"Because of heavy clouds and dew point issue, we could only ran two in-dome CBP tests". Louvers opened 00:16 UTC, closed 30 min later "because some temperatures of refrigerant line in the TMA was closed to the dew point (< 2 degC)". "At 03:01 UTC, outside dew point (-0.7 C) met dynalene temperature at Azimuth (-0.6 C)". "we decided not to open the dome tonight". Thick clouds all night. First night of the Dynalene/dew-point condensation policy.

"Clear skies, variable seeing". "The temperature difference between the dew point and the Dynalene_at_Az sensor… was less than 2 °C, so the dome remained closed. Once the difference exceeded 2 °C, the dome was opened at 03:50 UTC." Closed 8:39 UTC. In-dome flats/CBP before opening. MTMount fault (OBS-1491) needed realignment. Daytime attempt to raise Dynalene setpoint to 2 °C failed (OBS-1490) — condensation constraint is partly engineering.

"there were no weather-related delays today. Only minor issues for the night." Initial alignment 00:46–01:47 UTC, "Had to be repeated due a rotator issue - CCW telemetry is too old (OBS-922)"; FBS 06:20–08:30 UTC; dome closed 08:36 UTC. Seeing-limited (>1.1").

Clear. "There was a discussion for opening the dome in the sense of inside/outside dew point… (OBS-1479)"; "outside dew point dropped down quickly from 01:20 UTC… We opened the dome at 01:43 UTC" after visual inspection. Alignment 02:39–03:32 UTC, FBS 03:35–08:23 UTC; closed 08:35 UTC. "several Dome Az errors… easily recovered"; MTPtg/MTRotator fault 08:22 UTC (OBS-673). Late opening due to dew point.

"Simonyi was shutdown tonight due to various presence of liquid in several areas in and around the TMA… water condensation forming along different refrigeration lines". "High dewpoint temperatures delayed opening"; "kept it closed the entire night (8hrs observation time loss)". "At 2:26 UTC we had to recover another dynalene failure (FRACAS-823)… 1.57 hours." Clear sky, humidity 55–65%. Condensation = weather trigger on an engineering weakness (uninsulated Dynalene lines).

"Simonyi remained closed throughout the night due to the presence of liquid detected in several areas in and around the TMA. In addition… the +X mirror cover could not be opened" (OBS-1497). "High dew point temperatures prevented the opening of the telescope." "approximately 8 hours of observing time were lost." Outside dew point ~6.5 °C vs Dynalene 0.5 °C. Mixed.

"Due to high condensation on the exposed dynalene pipes (OBS-1479), we did not go on-sky tonight (weather time loss 8hrs)." In-dome super biases 23:44–3:05 UTC and PTC 3:43–8:30 UTC with +X mirror cover still stuck (OBS-1497). "At 7:10 UTC, M1M3 faulted… (OBS-1498, 0.53hrs lost for recovery)." Humidity >75% at night, clouds S and W.

Ambiguous. "Mostly a smooth night operations with closed dome and only PTC curve test performed until the dawn." No explicit reason given for staying closed: evening "outside and inside dew point increased to 5.3C and 4.3C", "prepared for the Camera tests", mirror cover X+ still stuck (verified pending next day). "During nighttime the dew point dropped up to ~ -7°C for around 4 hours." MTCamera fault 08:44 UTC (OBS-1499), two M1M3TS faults (OBS-1344). Likely condensation precaution + planned camera PTC + mirror cover.

Clear. Dew point–Dynalene difference 1–2 °C at sunset, "keeping the TMA at low elevations (<45°)". EtherCAT fault with MTDome before alignment (01:34 UTC); encoder head faults 02:42 UTC; "at 04:58 UTC, a rotator fault stopped the BLOCK-T667… repeated MTMount faults related to the azimuth position… Due to the time lost, we were only able to complete v2 of BLOCK-T667". Closed 08:45 UTC.

"Clear skies the whole night… dewpoints diff >9°C, no condensation risk". Dome opened 00:25 UTC, alignment 00:56 UTC, closed 08:31 UTC. M1M3 thermal mismatch and "M1M3TS connection faults with the glycol system" affected image quality; M1M3TS set to STANDBY; poor seeing (~1.3") → FBS poor-seeing then T667_v3. No explicit loss.

"both daytime systems verification and night observations went smoothly." Alignment 00:57 UTC, T667 v4/v5 01:44–, FBS 05:16–8:41 UTC. "Unbelievable but true. No alarms triggered during the whole night." Daytime faults only (locking pins OBS-1503, MTMount OBS-1197, ESS OBS-1189).

"Productive, quiet, and calm observation." "We opened the dome at 00:46 … The Mount remained at the horizon until the delta between Dewpoint and Dynalene … stabilized … We waited until the Delta T was consistently > 2°C" (condensation rule). FBS 02:24–08:42 UTC (≈1.5 h late start vs −12° twilight, dew-point wait). RH 4–8 %, wind < 4 m/s. OBS-564 is AuxTel.

Shutter open 00:13 UT; "Initial alignment started at Sun elevation -12 deg (00:51 UT)"; FBS from 01:26 UT. Faults: OBS-1483 "43 minutes time loss in total", OBS-965 "25 minutes time loss in total" (≈1.1 h fault). From 06:30 UTC scheduler overheads 10 s → 50 s. (Report says FBS "until 05.43 UT" but describes observing after 06:30 — inconsistent.) Warm, RH < 10 %, wind < 4 m/s.

Planned in-dome calibrations after camera firmware change (whitelight flats 00:20–01:37 UTC, darks); "collectively decided to deviate from doing more Darks and go onsky at 2:10 UTC." FBS first science 03:00–07:38 UTC, "On-sky for 4h." "At 5:40 UTC the Focalplane got stuck … Timeloss: 40min"; "At 7:38 UTC Cryoplate Trim Heat got very low (2.1W) … cut the last hour of the night" (camera, ≈1 h). Sky "very favorable". Early part planned (cals), later losses fault.
"Except for a 30 min hiccup, smooth night with FBS." FBS from 01:34 UTC; "FBS Downtime of 30 min from 5:34 to 05:55 UTC" (scheduler, OBS-1426); FBS stopped 08:46 UTC. RH ~45 %, wind < 5 m/s.

"FBS observations delayed/interrupted due environmental conditions." "Delayed beginning of on-sky due to outside dew point conditions for condensation at TEA … reverted at around 02:10 UT"; alignment 02:36 UT (≈1.7 h late). FBS 03:16–06:00 and 06:21–07:08 UT; "needed to close the dome shutter/louvers since outside dew point was reaching dynalene temperature" (≈1.7 h early close). "We closed twice Simonyi given risk of condensation." At 08:18 UTC, after closing, "several components went to fault … facility power in DP1 moved from about 144 Kv to 112 Kv … drop in current" — power glitch (OBS-1511), no on-sky loss. EAS faulted twice.

"We managed to salvage only 1 hr on-sky." Dew point "just around 2C (& oscillating!) colder than dynalene". "went on-sky 2 hrs late" (daytime condensation + camera trim heat). Alignment 02:40, FBS 03:20; "Dome closed at 03:48 UTC due to high humidity and dewpoint"; reopened 06:51; "closed again 07:31 UTC: large overheads … (L8 inspection, fault troubleshooting and slow scriptQs)"; FBS 08:03; end 08:32 UTC "a bit early due to dewpoint rise".

"smooth night, with few and short interruptions due to weather conditions and minor system issues." Twilight: TMA fault (OBS-1495), dome not following (OBS-1484, ~10 min). Alignment 01:27, FBS 02:05 UTC. "dome was closed at 05:30 UTC due to a low temperature difference (<2°C) … reopened at 06:05 UTC" (≈0.6 h weather). "07:50 UTC we had an MTMount fault … CCW following failure." End 08:50 UTC. Wind 7–12 m/s, RH peak 64 %.

"Simonyi operated at 20% performance with actuator 305 disabled." "no single issue caused prolonged time loss … more frequent minor issues". FA 305 recovery "delayed our on-sky time to around 1:00 UTC (0.75hrs lost)"; TMA fault "0.18 hrs lost" (OBS-1495); dome azimuth error 06:40 UTC "0.37hrs time loss" (OBS-646). ≈1.3 h fault total. FBS 02:04–08:50 UTC. "sudden increase in humidity in the late evening" hindered venting only.

"Night operations were delayed by environmental conditions." "Dome shutters and louvers were opened at 01:17 UTC due to dew point restrictions"; alignment 01:27, FBS 02:03 UTC (≈0.5–1 h late). "FBS observations ran smoothly with few interruptions." M1M3TS fault (OBS-1344), EAS failed, dome az error 08:42 UTC. Shutdown 08:48 UTC. Dew point 1.8–3.0 °C, RH ~50 %.

"Overall a smooth night … Minimal faults … did not cause any significant time loss. We started initial alignment at -10deg sun elevation … and observed until -12deg." Evening: Dynalene within ~0.2 °C of dew point, TMA kept at horizon until night (no stated night loss). EAS fault needing M1M3TS cRIO restart.

"Rapidly fluctuating dewpoint temperatures prevented us from observing most of the night. Condensation was found on the dynalene lines." "on-sky observations were postponed until around 7:11 UTC (6.40 hrs of time loss)." Closed 03:24, 05:45–06:12 UTC on dew-point spikes (−2.5 → 5.4 °C). Alignment 07:11–07:48, FBS 07:49–08:53 UTC. OBS-1493 "0.47hrs of recovery time … while we were closed due to weather."

"High dewpoint. FBS On sky for one hour." "At 03:53AM UTC the RH and dewpoint drops sharply. Shutter opened at 04:18AM UTC." Alignment 04:47–05:18; FBS 05:19–06:10 UTC "(stop at high dewpoint)"; M2 stray-light block skipped. In-dome dew point above 7 °C.

"3 hours of observation on a night with 75% humidity." "on sky around 02:30 UTC … until 05:20 UTC. The dew point was very high and the relative humidity reached 72%." Only issues: TMA "apply setting set"/"unpark" script errors slowing workflow. First data with new u filter.

"No MT observations were carried out during the night (time lost at 08:15). The dew point difference remained below 1 °C for most of the night … Visible condensation was confirmed … telescope remained parked at the horizon and no flats were taken." "could't go to high EL to open the mirror covers due to water condensation on TEA." Minor: compressor 2 off (OBS-1215). RH 55–75 %. AuxTel statement: closure "02:42" for humidity.

"Relatively smooth night, only ~1h loss due to dewpoint." Dome open 00:46 UTC; camera handed over 01:20 after OODS updates; on sky 01:50 UTC (≈1 h late, camera work + dew point). FBS 02:13–03:00 "(dewpoint break)", 04:25–08:50 UTC (≈1.4 h closed). "Second day we are running on generator due to scheduled commercial power cut. Power glitch caused short glycol cut" (OBS-1525); "Air compressor 2 down after a power glitch (FRACAS-227)". MTMount fault (OBS-1491). Power glitch flagged.

"A few hours of time lost early in the night due to high dewpoint. Lots of good FBS observations after that." "Slightly late start due to dewpoint delta <1.0C, then we had to close after initial alignment. Opened after another 1.5 hours." "Dewpoint difference oscillated around the 1.0C threshold for the first 2 hours." M1M3TS issue (OBS-1501) "did not interrupt FBS". FBS "until -12 twilight". No clock times given.

"A productive night with only minor issues. Total time lost was 48 minutes due to a recurrent MTAOS fault (OBS-1532). No issues related to condensation or weather were observed." Whole night FBS "starting with Sun elevation -13".

"we couldn't take any science data till 03:40 UTC due to mainly OBS-1535 … Time loss was 5 hours in total." Dome open 00:05 UTC; alignment attempts 00:37–03:36; "hexapod compensation mode didn't work well after camera hexapod went to fault at 00:25 UTC … (Time loss : 3h 3m)"; FBS 03:40–07:09 UTC ("onsky observation in total = 3.5 hours"); image-processing failure OBS-1538 "(time loss : 1h 50m)", shutdown 08:40 UTC, cals skipped. Humidity ~50 % stable.

"Smooth night of FBS observations plus two executions of an AOS test. Minor faults sprinkled throughout the night." "We were granted permission to override the dewpoint criteria after inspection showed the system to be dry; otherwise we would have lost the first four hours." Dome opened at −6° (temperature criterion). Ended at −12°; dome parking trouble (OBS-646), minimal cals failed to configure (OBS-1542). "Clear and calm all night."

"We lost the whole night because of a Dynalene outage at 00:39 UTC. (OBS-1546)" Recovered 04:10 UTC "(took 3.5 hours)", flow lost again, recovered 08:24 UTC. "we shut down nearly all the systems of MTCamera for safety." TMA parked at horizon 05:10 UTC, mirror covers left open. ESS 401–403 faults (OBS-1544). RH 50–60 %, wind ~3 m/s (no weather closure stated).

"No observing with Simonyi tonight due to ongoing efforts to restore LSSTCam from last night's dynalene incident. The TMA is locked out at horizon." Day log: dynalene issue "appeared to be related to a software issue and power-glitch handling rather than the cooling hardware itself" (power glitch mentioned, flagged). 02:23 UTC both air compressors lost pressure (OBS-974). AuxTel statement: "Very little observing … high relative humidity (>70%). Total time loss = 7 hr 14 min."

"LSSTCamera is unavailable due to dynalene loss and partial warmup. No tests or observing with Simonyi as it is under LOTO for pumping." AuxTel statement: "Minimal observing … high relative humidity (>70%). Total time loss = 5.2 hours."

"Only AuxTel observing tonight." "Camera was offline the entire day due to previous dynalene issues, so we will not be on-sky tonight." M1M3TS faults, glycol mixing valve recovery (OBS-1554). AuxTel statement: "~1 hour lost due to high relative humidity" (04:32–05:34 UTC).

"Simonyi observations continued to be suspended for LSSTCamera warmup (OBS-1546)." Dynalene cRIO being swapped. OSS remote fault / thermal-system cabinet issues (OBS-1217). AuxTel statement: "lost ~2+ hours due to high humidity."

"Simonyi continued with downtime due to camera warmup and dynalene issues." "A thunderstorm shook the summit after 21h local time … we remained in foggy conditions for the rest of the night" (RH > 88 %, low clouds) — would have closed Simonyi anyway. AuxTel statement: "lost a full night of observing due to stormy weather and high humidity."

"No observation due to Camera Cooldown." "All 6 oil cyro circuits started at 18:30 UTC … The process takes at least 8 hours." ESS 40x faults (OBS-1557). Night "calm, clear and humid but well below 70% RH".

"Great effort from the whole team to successfully go on sky tonight!!" "Night was a bit bumpy with Rotator, TMA faults and a LSSTCam Meltdown." Alignment 00:52–01:11 UTC ("Timeloss: 22min", camera noise discussion); BLOCK-T559 filter LUT 01:11–05:45 with TMA az-limit carousel "Timeloss: 53min" and four MTRotator faults "Timeloss: 40min" (OBS-1156); donut test 05:45–06:25 ("Timeloss: 10min"); FBS 06:35–08:30; closed 08:50 UTC, "15min earlier than -12 deg" (mirror-cover doubt, OBS-1046); cals cancelled "spontaneous LSSTCam Meltdown" (OBS-1558). ≈2.1 h fault. "Very dry and clear night."

"Night operations were impacted by technical issues by different subsystems (MTAOS, MTDome, MTRotator, and MTMount), affecting most of the night plan." FBS started at −13°; BLOCK-T559 v7 from 01:00 CLT with MTRotator/MTAOS faults; MTMount AXES PXI fault "could not be resolved" (OBS-1560). "we decided to shutdown Simonyi at 08:08 UTC" (≈0.7 h early), TMA left at el 74°. Clear skies; RH ~60 %, dew point > 5.5 °C, no closure stated.

"No observing with Simonyi tonight due to the vacuum issues with LSSTCamera." Day: TMA "stuck at el= 74 from the AXES PXI issue" (OBS-1560; FRACAS-337), OS updates 13:00–16:38 UTC delayed pump-cart work. RH 15–40 % at night, wind < 10 m/s.

"No on sky observations with Simonyi tonight due to the LSSTCam vacuum situation. The night was used to run dome thermalization tests" (BLOCK-T679/T681, 02:25–07:39 UTC; in-dome, dome open). Camera team: "ion pumps are not the source of anomalous output … leak detection". Clear, RH dropped to 6 %.

"No observations with Simonyi tonight. Daytime work was dedicated to the camera. The TMA remains with the trapped key overnight." Venting tests BLOCK-T679/T681 00:45–07:30 UTC; "03:00 UTC BLOCK execution abandoned due to dome closures (humidity)". "relative humidity spikes kept us on our toes." OSS faults (OBS-1267). AuxTel statement: closed for RH > 70 %, then ATMCS az-velocity faults (OBS-1268).

"Simonyi could not observe tonight due to previous issues with LSSTCam (8hrs time loss)" — cryo vacuum pressure rising, "suggests a leak". Off-sky tests also removed "as a conservative approach to the unstable weather forecasts"; night "clear … but with very high humidity (>70%)". OSS run 23:00–03:15 UTC.

"Simonyi could not observe tonight due to previous issues with LSSTCam (8hrs time loss). Off-sky dome tests were not run either due to high humidity during the night." Humidity >70% first half, spike >80% ~07:45 UTC. AuxTel lost 4.5 h to humidity (AuxTel statement).

Camera leak (no Simonyi on-sky). Night "Humidity mostly > 80 %" (AuxTel open only 10 min — AuxTel statement). "Brief power cut at dinner time … glycol/dynalene cut off for ~1 minute. OSS faulted" — power glitch. "Around 6:30 UTC, night OS crew left the observatory" (staffing; approved by Kevin Reil). OSS 22:14–05:39 UTC.

"Simonyi could not observe tonight due to previous issues with LSSTCam (8hrs time loss)." Dome tests only: BLOCK-T679 01:57–08:25 UTC, shutter closed 02:58 UTC for humidity (~75%), restarted ~04:25 UTC.
"Simonyi remained shut down due to the camera vacuum leak." "Venting and dome thermal tests were run all night without issue." Weather: "closure limits were never exceeded".
"No Simonyi observations due to LSSTCam vacuum leak (FRACAS-338)." Dome tests BLOCK-T681 and T679; OSS off 03:22 UTC. "Low humidity and wind speed."

"LSSTCam is still offline due to the vacuum leak (FRACAS-338)." Dome opened 01:11 UTC for tests T679 01:15–04:16, T687 04:16–08:29; closed 08:30 UTC. M1M3/TS fault 08:38 UTC from GIS e-stop, recovered 10:15 UTC.
"Night without LSSTCam because of vacuum leak (FRACAS-338)." Dome tests T679 00:11–03:14 UTC, T681 03:18–07:22 UTC. Wind <5 m/s all night.

"Simonyi could not observe tonight due to LSSTCam being offline to seal the cryo vacuum leak (~9hrs time loss)." Dome tests T679 23:30–04:32 UTC, T681 04:45–08:55 UTC; closed 09:00 UTC. Mostly clear, RH 50–60%.

"Simonyi could not observe tonight due to LSSTCam being offline to seal the cryo vacuum leak (8hrs time loss)." Dome tests T684 00:08–04:29, T679 04:40–08:40 UTC; closed 08:45 UTC. TMA ETPB / El lim+ interlocks 08:48–09:45 UTC not recovered. Clear, wind 1–3 m/s.

"Simonyi: Dome tests only." Camera leak continues. "Brief power cut at the beginning of the night … commercial power was restored after ~5 minutes" — power glitch. Tests T685 01:15–05:32 UTC, T681 05:34–07:40 UTC. Clear, winds <2 m/s.

"Simonyi: Dome tests only." Daytime: "Successful attempt of the Vacuum Seal"; 6.2-mag earthquake ~13:39 UTC, systems recovered. Dome tests T681 00:12–04:02 UTC (interrupted, gusts 9 m/s), T679 06:30–08:30 UTC.
"Simonyi/LSSTCam remained at horizon." Camera REBs turned on 17:15 UT. Night: OSS 4 h and dome thermal tests T679/T681. TMA az/el thermal systems in fault (OBS-1590). 8% humidity.
"Simonyi: Dome tests only." Camera "getting ready for the pump cart removal + testing tomorrow". BLOCK-T681 v2 run twice; winds 1–4 m/s.

Camera recommissioning night after the leak: "Camera vacuum stabilization was confirmed by camera team at 02:34 UTC"; "At 03:25 UTC, calibration attempts … switched to SuperBias"; "Camera went to FAULT at 04:34 UTC (OBS-1597) and recovered at 05:00 UTC"; SuperBias completed 08:40 UTC, then parked. No on-sky. Partly planned recovery, partly fault (leak follow-on, fiber spectrographs). Clear, wind 2 m/s.
"We are back on-sky!" BLOCK-T288 then FBS; "AOS mis-configuration (OBS-1603) that cost 1 hour"; "5 hours of uninterrupted FBS observations" then stray-light BLOCK-T676. Clear and calm. ≈1 h lost.

"Unfortunately we lost the night due to a major camera firmware issue that caused an unexpected ~60 W increase in focal plane power after the glycol outage" (all 4 glycol chillers lost during the day, FRACAS-344). Also OSS faults from El lim+ interlock (OBS-1511) and EIB error. Clear, RH <10%.

"Back on sky with the first FBS with Alerts!" Dome opened 23:30 UTC; FBS from 01:08 UTC; pointing model 02:36–04:14 UTC with dome fault "lost about 20 minutes"; scheduler/camera error 06:37 UTC (OBS1613) cleared; end 10:00 UTC. RH ~8%, wind ~4 m/s.

"on-sky all night with just few minor issues." FBS 00:34 UTC; MTMount az fault "time loss ~45 minutes" (OBS-959); re-running initial alignment "time loss ~60 minutes"; "5:00 UTC clouds started to form in the West … only <1 mag extinction … we continued". ≈1.75 h lost to faults.

"Dew point higher than the operational limit throughout the entire night prevented us from opening the dome … we lost the total 09:10 hours." "difference to Dynalene <-4C almost entire night"; "a lot of water condensation on all non-insulated Dynalene pipes". Dew point ~8 °C, RH 70–75%.

"Another night off-sky … condensed water on the TMA and Dynalne pipes prevented us from unparking the telescope from horizon. Total time loss was the entire night, 09:10 hours." Dew-point limit reached ~04:00 UTC, vented until 06:00 UTC, "still a lot of water accumulated". M1M3 FA 334 faults were daytime.

"Rubin Alerts FBS night." FBS from 00:27 UTC; "LSSTCam focal-plane issue (OBS-1628) … time loss 00:36 hr"; four MTAOS and two MTRotator faults "did not cause delays". "at least ~8 hrs of on-sky time". Dew point to Dynalene difference >−2 °C.

"FBS on sky all night." On sky 00:30 UTC. "CCW faulted … 20m time loss"; MTAOS faults 04:40, 07:35, 09:24 UTC; MTDome ERROR 06:29, 08:00, 08:17 UTC; M1M3 fault at end of night. RH ~50%, wind <1 m/s most of night.

"First Public alerts night! … on-sky for ~ 8.5 hrs (637 science visits)." Alignment from 00:06 UTC (third attempt, OBS-738); FBS 00:30 UTC; "7:00 UTC — CCW timeout caused MTMount to fault … Dome … errors … cost us 30 min"; FBS stopped 09:26 UTC, closed 09:31 UTC. RH 52%, winds dying.

"After a delayed start on sky due to dew point constraints and dome opening errors, we got on sky around 02:45 UT." "CCW telemetry failures … cost about 2 hours, and the dome failure in OBS-1644 which delayed us getting on sky by almost 2 hours." Weather: "Dewpoint … reaching a diff with predicted dynalene of -2°C, opening limit. We suffered a bit of weather loss at the start of the night". Dome would not close at end of night. Weather and dome fault overlap at the start; ≈2 h start delay + ≈2 h CCW.

"Smooth night except for frequent MTAOS faults." FBS from 00:30 UTC. "MTAOS faulted 8 times (OBS-1629)"; CCW fault (OBS-1645); MTDome error once. "Power glitch at 08:12UTC and 08:57UTC. Generators ran for a few minutes" — power glitch; MTAircompressor 2 went off. Calibration skipped (fiber spectrographs). Good weather, wind <3 m/s. No hours stated.

"We ran the FBS survey the whole night"; FBS 00:16–09:38 UTC; "around 1.34hrs of time loss" from MTDome az drives (0.51 h, OBS-646), MTMount axes (0.43 h, OBS-959), LSSTCam resumeGuiding fault 03:15 UTC (0.4 h, OBS-1653). Daytime "power glitch in the morning" affecting CalSys — power glitch (daytime only). Closed 09:45 UTC. Clear, wind 1–4 m/s.

"Aside from a MTMount fault, the telescope was well behaved. We lost a bit of sky time with the scheduler getting into a 'stuck' state". "quite a bit of time repeating alignment to improve PSF" (AOS strategy, not weather: "all environmental factors indicated good seeing"). Calm, wind <3 m/s. No hours stated.

"We ran only FBS tonight." Dome/louvers open 23:55/00:03 UTC; FBS 00:38–09:40 UTC; close 09:45 UTC. "8 time MTDome Az Drive error events (OBS-646) … reboot MTDome cRIO at 01:16 UTC. The time lost in total is 0.45 hours." MTAOS timeouts 04:29/04:44 UTC; MTMount overspeed alarm 09:49 UTC while parking (OBS-1656). Weather mild (wind 2–5 m/s, ~40 %). Daytime: "16h UTC: Commercial outage. The Mitsubishi generator takes over" — chillers 1/2 not responding, controlled quickly (daytime power event, no night loss).

"Observing was delayed by over two hours at the beginning of the night due to troubleshooting from the DevOps team" — "kubernetes issue … Yagan8 node … Nexus server … expired license (2.10hrs time loss)". Alignment 00:10–02:42 UTC (re-run 02:34); FBS 02:45–05:59; shutter timing test 06:03–06:28; DDS 06:46–09:41 UTC; closed 09:46 UTC. Dome Az stuck (OBS-646, 0.12 h); MTPtg/MTRotator fault 07:43 UTC (OBS-922). "Weather was clear during the night."

"The night proceeded smoothly with minimal issues and only 9 minutes of downtime for Simonyi." FBS "covered all night"; dome error 00:40 UTC (no time lost); MTMount/MTPtg fault 05:59 UTC (9 min, OBS-959). EGW pump lost on the evening, flow low all night, recovered 10:06 UTC (no loss stated). "Clear skies", wind < 5 m/s. AuxTel: ATCamera fault 08:20 UTC, 1 h 20 m lost (AuxTel statement).

"No simonyi onsky tonight because of engineering works. Three in-dome tests performed." Planned: "MTCamera and Simonyi are not going back online for tonight" (Dynalene cRIO swap, CCS DB server migration, M1M3 thermal update). Dome opened for thermal-gradient / louver tests 23:40–04:01 and 06:15–09:22 UTC. Dome Az errors ×5 (OBS-646), capacitor alarms (OBS-1627), LOVE redis slow (OBS-1668). Thick clouds after 06:30 UTC (AuxTel statement).

Daytime "summit OS updates and k8s upgrades … kafka brokers took three hours to recover, so the control system became available starting at 21:55 UTC" (planned, daytime). Dome handover 23:08 UTC. Night: "Recover From Controller Fault had several executions: 02:22, 02:32, 02:34, 02:37, 03:33, 04:42, 05:56, 06:37, 06:49, 07:20" (OBS-646); "FBS continued working in the background, which produced vignetting in some images." Calibrations failed to load schema. No on-sky hours lost stated; ambiguous. Wind < 6 m/s.

"It was a bumpy night." In-dome: "A configuration error in the flat-field acquisition script resulted in a 1 hour and 26 minute delay, blocking the time window for the PTC test" (OBS-1674). On sky: T694 stray light, T637 exposure scan ("FBS observations were delayed by 20 minutes" after M1M3 TS fault, OBS-1675), FBS T624 (one MTPtg/MTAOS fault), T676 "camera fault provoked by a filter change that make us lose 40min (OBS-1676)". ≈2.4 h lost, all technical. Evening humidity > 60 % then 45–60 %, wind 0–5 m/s, seeing < 1″ after 06 UTC.

"We observed for ~3 hours total. Operations stopped due to high humidity and later thick cloud cover (≈7 hours lost)." Alignment 00:08–00:40 UTC; FBS 00:41–02:47; "02:47 UTC – Dome closed due to high humidity (~75%) and overcast"; in-dome PTC 03:00–09:47; "07:22 UTC – Dome opened; humidity <70% for ~30 min"; FBS resumed 07:43; "08:26 UTC – Dome closed due to thick clouds; MTAOS faulted twice." Humidity 57–89 %, winds to 15–17 m/s after 08:45 UTC. Daytime: "power glitch at 20:44 UTC. MT air compressor 2 down … Glycol went low for a few minutes"; M1M3 glycol pump failed 16:30–20:24 UTC (daytime).

"Simonyi, AuxTel, and DIMM.1 observed all night." Alignment 00:08–00:21 UTC "Seeing ~2.1″, thick clouds and humidity ~70%"; FBS 00:22–09:45 UTC, "Seeing improved to ~1.0-1.1″ for most of the night". "OBS-646 — Dome AZ fault (~30 min lost)"; "OBS-1680 — MTAOS fault … (~6 min lost)"; "OBS-1217 — TMA main cabinet fault, could not be reset" (time not stated); M1M3TS glycol flow lost 7 min (OBS-1114). "First half it was very cloudy, improving in the second half" — observed through it.

"Observations started at 00:20 UTC after initial alignment. MTMount and MTPtg faulted around 00:30 UTC due to a positive operational software limit. Restarting the PXIs and PIlz did not resolve the issue, resulting in ~3 hours of on-sky time loss. The issue was eventually bypassed, and continued with the FBS survey." Dynalene off 06:41–06:54 UTC (OBS-1686); dome Az errors (OBS-646). Weather: wind ~3.75 m/s, ~45 %. Daytime: "power glitch event at 13:59 UTC for about 1 min … generator power back automatically" (no effect).

"Simonyi, AuxTel, and DIMM.1 observed all night." Closed Loop Stability test (BLOCK-T641) 00:15–09:30 UTC. "Dome AZ fault occurred 10 times … the telescope was pointing in the same direction throughout the night, so the issue did not significantly affect observations." close_loop failures (OBS-1689/1690); minimal cals failed 09:48 UTC (OBS-1692/1693). Thin clouds, wind 1–7 m/s.

"Overall the night was mostly successful with normal observing operations." FBS closed-loop stability from 00:00 UTC; "several system faults occurred but were generally recovered quickly"; "Around 06:00 UTC … the glycol pump was not running, we recovered and continue observing" (OBS-1114); dome closed 09:00 UTC; white-light flats aborted (Electrometer 103 fault, OBS-1099, in-dome). "Clear skies and generally good weather", seeing 0.8″.

Alignment done ~23:55 UTC; "FBS-driven closed-loop stability test started at ~00:04 UTC" and "ran smoothly until 04:20 UTC"; MTAOS RA-timeout faults "did not interrupt the obs"; stray light test and white-light flats for 5 filters afterwards (planned in-dome; summary says flats done ~07:00 UTC, Simonyi section says stray light 07:30–07:47 and flats ~10:00 UTC — inconsistent `[check]`). Dome Az errors 23:07/23:20 UTC (OBS-646). Humidity ~22 %, wind ~1.4 m/s. AuxTel did not observe (dome shutter, OBS-1703 — AuxTel statement).

"Operations were delayed due to the mirror inspections required after the morning earthquake" (13:40 UTC, M6.5 Huasco; M1M3 HP forces oscillated ±3000 N for 2+ h, FRACAS-363). Night shift from ~21:00 UTC for HP breakaway tests and cell inspections; "EWG leak detection" interlock from a disconnected plug (OBS-1704); camera fault at first filter exchange (OBS-1705). "On sky operations Initial Alignment and FBS stability test ran from 04:30–08:05 UTC." ≈5 h lost at start to earthquake safety checks (neither weather nor fault); the interlock and camera fault added delay. No clouds; humidity 70 % at sunset falling to 50 %.

"Observations tonight were smooth despite the MTAOS CSC faults." "We were ready to start venting since about 22.20 UT but humidity is at around 70% and we are not in the operational limit for opening the dome"; L8 condensation check (RH ~65 %, no condensation). Alignment 00:29–00:49 UTC; FBS closed-loop 00:50–09:51 UTC "(Total time lost: 0.33h)": encoder Az head 1 lost (OBS-1445, 0.18 h), MTAOS faults (OBS-1532, 0.15 h). RH ~60 %, seeing < 0.9″. Humidity-delayed opening ≈ 0.5–1 h.

"The initial observation time was a bit bumpy due to FCS issues, the time spent for this recovery was 1.04h." Alignment 23:41–23:50 UTC; T614 00:03–00:42 "(1.04h time lost)" — filter telemetry mismatch, MCM restart (OBS-1708, after FES fault OBS-1707); re-alignment 01:47–02:01; T614 02:04–06:08 (0.13 h, wrong rotator config); T703 06:11–09:53 UTC (0.16 h). OSS faulted 10:18 UTC (OBS-942). ≈1.3 h lost, technical. Clear, RH ~55 %, wind < 10 m/s.

"At the beginning of the night, clouds caused some problems during observations, but they dissipated quickly." Alignment 23:47 UTC; T703 00:00–07:48 UTC "(~0.9h weather time lost)" — "the clouds prevented us from perceiving stars, covering everything between 00:41 and 01:50 UTC"; T614 07:52–09:54 UTC. "The left workstation … I was unable to observe for ~50 min (OBS-1714)" (observer station, telescope impact unclear). Seeing 1.0–2.0″, wind 6–10 m/s.

"Alignment issues from a new pipeline prevented convergence; manual focus helped but image quality remained insufficient, so key blocks were not run. Reverted to previous configuration after 1.7 hours of troubleshooting." T614 01:40–05:50 UTC (OBS-1720 close_loop failed 3×, 0.5 h lost); T703 05:50–09:52 UTC (OBS-1532 MTAOS timeout, 0.17 h). ≈2.4 h lost, software/config. "Clear and stable night", wind < 6 m/s, 30 %.

"very good night, no issues, just DATA!" "No Faults... just Dome ethercat OBS-646 (2 times)". T698 from 00:14 UTC, T706 from 03:37 UTC. "Clear and calm", seeing 0.7–1.2″. Daytime: FA 415 air leak (OBS-1723), workstation 2 failed (OBS-1443).

"Simonyi lost the last 6h due to a PCS chiller error (OBS-1727)." Alignment 23:38–00:18 UTC; T706 00:22–03:02; T379 03:07–03:38; T378 started 03:40; "3:58 UTC PCS chiller E2_COMPRESSOR1_FAIL … could not be restarted, LSSTCam remains OFFLINE … (Time lost ~6h)". Dome Az fault ×10 (OBS-646); significant dome seeing (warm M1M3). "Cold windy night", humidity 55–83 %, wind 8–13 m/s — AuxTel lost 2.2 h to humidity (AuxTel statement).

"No observing tonight with Simonyi due to PCS chiller failure yesterday … NO OBSERVATIONS." Camera crew installed the pump cart; vacuum monitored all night. Weather also bad: "Highly unstable weather conditions. Humidity remained above 70% for most of the time … cloud cover … dense during the second half" (AuxTel opened only ~30 min). Minor earthquake 03:58 CLT, no consequences. Daytime: air compressor 2 down 14:15–17:53 UTC; chillers 1 and 3 failed and recovered (OBS-1729).

"No Simonyi observations tonight. Camera team continues to investigate the leak." TMA parked at horizon with pump cart connected; He leak test in the evening; M1M3 thermalization test (T697) at horizon; "8:15 UTC M1M3TS glycol pump failed (OBS-1114)". "Mostly clear skies", wind 5–15 m/s.

"Off-sky night" — "Camera still off" (vacuum leak). M1M3 thermalization test 23:55–08:55 UTC with "several more faults of the glycol pump" (OBS-1114, OBS-1732). Cloudy until 02:00 UTC then clear; cold, wind decreased at night. AuxTel closed for S3 endpoint issue (OBS-1731 — AuxTel statement).

"We did a few steps of the vacuum test T688" (camera recovery, LSSTCam still off-sky). "There is some planned work going on with dome shutter so we are not able to open the dome shutter." TMA Az blocked by an unreleased LOTO after walkaround (OBS-1734); "decided to stop here due to the lack of emergency camera support (Yousuke is sick)". Mixed: camera fault recovery dominant, plus planned shutter work and staffing. Clear, RH ~19 %, wind ~8 m/s.

"On-sky AOS stability verification, ASCT-004 Bending tests, and FBS with Louver testing. … Camera vacuum pressure remained stable for the night." T614 from 01:03 UTC; T378 02:24 (postponed, thermal donut patterns); T706/T696 03:08–07:00; T378 07:01–07:47; T379 07:47–08:13; T614 08:18–08:28 "when we lost MTCamera Heartbeat because we lost lsstcam-mcm1 computer" (OBS-1738, end of night). Dome errors (OBS-646); M1M3 glycol pump comm loss (OBS-1732); minimal cals failed (OBS-1737). "Dry night … almost no wind."

"Simonyi and AuxTel had quite smooth onsky night with minor issues." Alignment 23:38 UTC; T709 23:54–02:00; T710 02:02–02:48; T614 03:07–04:25; T460 04:41–06:37; T614 07:01–09:13 UTC; shutdown 09:14 UTC. MTM1M3 fault 01:25 UTC (OBS-1732), one apply_dof failure. Off-band LED flats skipped (ESS:404 / LEDProjector faults, OBS-1216/1741). Humidity 25–35 %, wind rising to 10 m/s.

"MCM1 crashed 100 times. We decided to close for the night and keep monitoring. ~4 hours time loss." Alignment 23:33–23:47 UTC; T701 TMA-fan test 23:47–05:15 (fan status uncertain); T614 05:15–05:35; "mcm1 crashed at 05:35 … again at 06:13 and 06:40 (and a lot more later) … we decided to close for the night." Dome errors ×6, MTAOS 01:30, M1M3TS 03:06/04:25 UTC. RH ~40 %, wind < 4 m/s.

"Electrifying day but quite satisfying night." "today we spent 0.6 hours for initial alignment" (tried without set_dof); T708 00:26–01:36; T710 01:53–02:30; T614 02:33–08:21 UTC (5 positions); FBS 08:47–09:35 (scheduler double filter change OBS-1744, MTAOS fault 08:48 UTC OBS-1735, restarted 09:09); LED flats 09:50 UTC. Daytime: "15:41 UTC: Power outage. Generators activated … Glycol Chiller 1 setpoint changed (OBS-1743)"; "22:19 UTC: second power outage" — daytime power events, no night loss. Wind 5–6 m/s, 32–35 %.

"Calm day and a good night … running Scheduler for the entire night (~8.98h) despite of M2 hexapod interruption." Alignment 23:30–23:45 UTC; T701 23:47–00:59; "00:59 - 01:34 UTC: Scheduler in fault, it cannot find next target. The reason was the moon being too close … (0.63h time lost)"; re-alignment 01:34–01:42; T701 resumed 01:44 UTC with repeated M2 Hexapod timeouts (OBS-1697). LED flats 09:43–10:23 UTC. No clouds, RH ~35 %, wind 2–5 m/s.

"Operational the entire night with both Simonyi and AuxTel. The Feature Based Scheduler was run for the entire night. Several ethercat connection issues with the MTDome, however minimal time on-sky was lost." Opened 23:00 UTC; closed 09:15 UTC; off-band flats blocked by electrometer timeouts (OBS-1748). Humidity ~30 %, low wind.

"Simonyi and AuxTel were fully functional throughout the night. We ran The Feature Based Scheduler with TMA fans on for 10.5h." Alignment 23:47–00:15 UTC; FBS 00:28–10:01 UTC. "06:40 UTC: Power glitch. The observatory's machinery responds to the problem (Generator, Dynalene) … No issues to report related to the cooling system, M1M3, or the camera" — DREAM faulted (OBS-1749). Power glitch flagged, no observing loss. RH < 31 %, wind < 3 m/s.

"On-sky time lost for both Simonyi and AuxTel due to faults." T668 TARTS, T698 FBS closed-loop, then T614 "faced an issue of unknown cause with the rotator (OBS-1759). The test was somewhat successful, but it was ended early due to an OSS fault"; "No calibrations performed, TMA not parked at zenith." No clock times, hours lost not stated. Daytime: M1M3TS glycol pump failed 21:20 UTC (OBS-1114); dome Az faults (OBS-646). Clear, RH ~25 %, wind < 5 m/s.

"Smooth operations with the Simonyi systems, but suboptimal performance of the wavefront estimation." "We went on sky at 23:22 UTC"; BLOCK-T698 then T614 for the remainder of the night; "Rapid Analysis struggled to keep up (OBS-1765)". One dome Az ERROR at handover. Weather: RH < 30%, wind < 5 m/s. No time loss stated.

"Regular night with minor technical issues … with no significant time lost." On sky 23:38 UTC. "Several dome errors occurred, but no time was lost" (OBS-646); MTAOS restarted after a crash (OBS-1768); IQ degraded by M1M3 thermal gradients (OBS-1769). Warm, dry (RH 1.6%).

"Uneventful but a good night"; on sky 23:37 UTC, "We were on-sky for at least 10 hrs", stopped at −12.3° twilight (10:02 UTC). Dome "cascade … of ethercat connection problems" but no loss stated. Wind "stable high winds up to 15 m/s"; AuxTel stopped 09:21 UTC "due to winds" (AuxTel statement). Off-band LED flats abandoned (Electrometer.103, OBS-1771).

"With Simonyi, we lost 1.35 hours in total due to MTAOS high-load issue (0.73 h, OBS-1774) and scheduler issue (0.62 h, Moon distance < 30°)." Initial alignment 23:39 UTC, shutdown 10:02 UTC. 85 MTAOS heartbeat alerts (OBS-896); glycol pump offline 04:51–08:25 UTC (OBS-1114). "Another windy night", wind to 17 m/s first half; AuxTel closed 00:55–02:06 UTC for wind (AuxTel statement). No calibrations (OBS-1771).

"The entire night was dedicated to [pre-LSST FBS, from 23:55 UTC], with only minor issues: There were 5 MTMount faults, followed by an MTPtg fault (OBS-641) … total time lost … approximately 30 minutes." MTAOS alarms every 2 min (OBS-896); no calibrations (OBS-1771). Clear skies, wind < 10 m/s, RH < 55%.

"Good Night! Bad Mount … the mount encoders was the only persistent issue"; "MTMount failed several times (OBS-1445)" — no duration given. "6:22 UTC We experienced a momentary power outage. Both generators kicked in … No systems were affected. Observations even continued during the outage." Daytime power glitch 18:08 UT (chiller 2 stopped ~1 min). Seeing ~2″ early. Power glitch flagged; loss ambiguous.

"A very quiet night, without any major problems." Pre-LSST survey from 23:31 UT. Losses listed: MTDome ethercat "20min in total" (OBS-646), MTAOS crash "30min lost" (OBS-1768), "MTScheduler.1 got OOM killed, 1h lost" (OBS-1782) — ≈1.8 h total. OSS faulted at start (OBS-1776). Wind 8–10 m/s, RH ~22%.

"Great night, just 1 fault of the OSS" at 08:31 UTC (OBS-1785). Survey from 23:44 UTC. "MTDome got stuck and does not follow TMA (OBS-646) … 18m time loss on sky." Seeing 0.7″ stable. OS/k8s update during the day.

"The night, issues with the Dome multiple times (x11), M1M3 fault (x2) and OSS fault." Exposure scan from 23:33 UTC, FBS 02:20 UTC, AOS triplets 04:40–~09:40 UTC. No hours lost stated — ambiguous. Seeing "very unstable from 1 to 2 arcseconds"; wind 3–5 m/s.

"Several faults of M1M3 due to a following error of FA 322 lost 1.8 hours of on-sky time (OBS-1791)" (02:07 UTC 49 min, 06:14 UTC 47 min, 07:48 UTC 15 min) + MTPtg/scheduler fault 03:40 UTC "approx. 25 min" (OBS-1792) — ≈2.2 h. FBS from 23:30 UTC "for the entire night"; glycol pump off most of the night. "High wind speeds 10-17 m/s"; AuxTel closed 09:25 UTC for wind (AuxTel statement).

"Mostly a smooth night. Simonyi ran FBS survey for most of the night." Dome opened 22:44 UTC, FBS 23:32–07:11 UTC, stray-light test 07:15–07:40, FBS resumed to end of night. "MTDome Az fault occurred 5 times during the night, we lost 13 minutes." M1M3TS fault ~09:00 UTC (OBS-1501). Clear skies, wind 4–11 m/s.

"Night operations were impacted by clouds at ~08:50 UTC, finishing observations at ~09:13 UTC." "At 09:11 UTC scheduler failed due to clouds. We stopped the scheduler at 09:13 UTC." Science from 23:30 UTC. ≈1 h lost to clouds at the end. Faults with no stated loss: 3 dome Az errors, CCW timeout (OBS-1467), MTPtg/MTRotator (OBS-922), MTMount Az overspeed (OBS-1800).

"We observed for only ~5.5 hours due to thick clouds." FBS 23:37–~04:15 UTC "we had to stop due to thick clouds"; "Dome closed at 4:34 UTC"; re-opened 06:40, FBS 06:43–07:35 UTC "due to clouds"; "Dome closed at 7:43 UTC"; closed-dome flats and M1M3 thermalization test after. "Cloudy night", RH 37–54%. ≈4.5 h lost to clouds.

"MTMount fault, M1M3 fault due to Mirror cell door Interlock and MTCamera focal plane issue caused 1.53 hrs time loss" (0.33 h OBS-1808, 0.43 h OBS-1797, 0.77 h OBS-1628). T698 00:20–02:40, pre-LSST 03:00–10:09 UTC. "Stable weather conditions with clear sky", wind ~4 m/s.

"We lost ~3 hours due to TMA issues, thermal system recovery, and a seismic event." MTRotator communication issue (OBS-1814) "we lost ~2.5 hrs (from -10° Sun's elevation to the Initial Alignment at 01:39 UTC)"; 02:04 UTC TMA thermal system inactive (0.12 h); 03:24 UTC seismic event (M 4.0) → M1M3 fault (0.43 h); then FBS for the rest of the night. Clear skies. Seismic loss counted under fault here.

"Observatory State: Downtime to allow the camera vacuum seal to cure." "Nighttime was spent running dome/louver tests (BLOCK-T679, ~04:30–09:45 UTC) and M1M3 thermal gradient tests (BLOCK-T719)." No on-sky. Downtime driven by the LSSTCam cryo vacuum leak (fault origin, scheduled repair). Clouds by ~09:00 UTC; AuxTel shut down 09:10 UTC (AuxTel statement).

"Observatory State: Downtime due to LSSTCam cryo vacuum leak investigation." "Camera team is still working on vac leak. Not going to on-sky." Dome/louver tests ~02:30–09:00 UTC and M1M3 thermal gradient test in-dome. Clear weather.

"LSSTCam cryo vacuum investigation and camera rotator pin troubleshooting delayed night observations by over 5 hours." "We officially began night operations around 4:17 UTC (~5hrs observing time loss)"; OSS slow to enable → chiller #2 restart (OBS-1818); rotator locking pin "~2.62hrs of the total time loss" (OBS-1819). AOS tests 04:27–10:06 UTC; "new image quality record" PSF FWHM 0.57″. Clear, seeing 0.5–0.8″.

"Priority of Simonyi movement demonstrations for guests at the summit delayed on-sky procedures to not start until around 00:15 UTC (~1 hr of time loss)" — neither weather nor fault (visitor demo). "Other than that we were on-sky with fewer issues"; ~15 min scheduler re-enable. M1M3TS glycol pump disabled all night (OBS-1820), thermal gradients out of limits. Mostly clear; AuxTel did not observe (visitor viewing).

"A calm and fairly productive night, with a sprinkling of known minor faults (OBS-646 Dome ethercat, OBS-641 TMA softmotion, OBS-922 CCW telemetry too late) costing around half an hour." Alignment 22:57 UTC. "We closed early to attempt the high-priority u-band monochromatic flats but problems with the laser tracker, calibration laser and scripts defeated our efforts. This ~1 hour of time loss at the end of the night was not captured as Fault time" (planned early close, then cal-system faults). RH 60–65%.

"Despite a rough start with a failing OSS which costed 1.66h observing time, mostly a smooth night." OSS caused MTMount fault (OBS-1828); "4 Dome AZ fault (OBS-646) 15min"; "CCW Pull Cord Fault (OBS-875) 20min" — ≈2.2 h total. Pre-LSST FBS to −12°. Clear sky, some cirrus early. Last night before Cycle 4 update.

"TMA PXI issues could not be resolved so Simonyi stayed off sky." "The dome was opened despite the inoperable TMA, and BLOCK-T679 (Dome venting - louver configuration test) was executed. TMA was recovered … around 5:30am." PXI lost network configuration after card swap (OBS-1834). Cycle 44 deployed on summit (planned) but the stated cause of no-sky is the PXI fault. Night mostly clear, low wind.

"Fairly smooth night despite a scattering of faults." On sky 23:03 UTC. "Recurring dome azimuth faults (0.25h)", "Rotator out of range (0.2h)", "Multiple TMA Mount FAULT (0.52h)" (OBS-641, home_both_axes failed ×5, OBS-992) — ≈1 h. "Due to clouds (CC 50%), we failed close_loop at 00:49 UTC (OBS-1690)"; "Scattered clouds affected some of the images early in the night, but they dissipated". Wind to 8–9 m/s late.

"First half of the night, the hexapod compensation modes were not working, images seq. 169 - 398 are corrupted. If we count this as time loss it would be 6.5 hr." Issue fixed 06:09 UT; "FBS restarted after issues were fixed at 06:14" until 10:12. "Three MTMount and MTPtg faults due to Az Encoder issues - total time loss ~0.4 hr" (OBS-965). Telescope was on sky all night; status reflects data loss, ambiguous whether to count. Clear sky, wind ~5 m/s.

Initial alignment ~22:56 UTC; "the scheduler was unable to load targets (OBS-1847, 1hr time loss)"; T698 from 00:56 UTC, FBS from 02:11 UTC. CCW fault (OBS-1645), MTMount fault at homing (OBS-965), homing "Time loss ~20m" (OBS-992); dome errors 05:56 and 09:58 UTC. Pneumatic louvers failed to open fully / close (OBS-1849). Wind < 3 m/s, RH ~6%. ≈1.3 h lost.

"Night Observations were delayed due to a camera issue for about 3.08h." "[00:06 UTC]: MCM entered in fault state. Controlled subsystem focal-plane has gone into FAULT (LSSTCAM-171). Time lost 3.08h." CamHex compensation mode could not be enabled 01:46 UTC (OBS-1249); alignment 02:57, FBS 04:12–10:41 UTC. MTMount/MTPtg faults (OBS-964, OBS-985). RH ~4%, wind ~2 m/s.

"Chaotic night … Thick clouds over the entire sky since 06:00 UTC. Dome closed at ~08:10 UTC. 1 hour time loss due to issues and 4 hours weather time loss." FBS first half with MTMount/MTPtg faults 00:40, 01:16, 02:07, 05:26, 07:20 UTC (~5 min each, OBS-985), MTCamera jGroup meltdown "36m time loss" (OBS-1558), camera hexapod "~20m". M1M3 glycol pump disabled (OBS-1836).
