"Both telescopes off-sky." "The camera glycol was in danger when we arrived at the control room (<2gpm; OBS-1876). It was soon rescued to a marginally safe situation"; monitored till 2AM CLT; "M1M3 Air compressor 2 stopped at ~4:28AM CLT … no success." Daytime: "Another power glitch at 15:38 lasted for about 18 seconds. Afterwards strange Glycol flow was detected. Caterpillar generator remained on" — power glitch. Weather: "DIMM.1 and DREAM remain DISABLED for tonight due to bad weather prediction"; night RH ~40%, wind < 2 m/s — weather was not the closure cause.

"No observations tonight. The camera glycol flow and cryos were monitored throughout the night. At approximately 07:00 UTC, Cryo 6 stopped … successfully recovered." Daytime: "Wind screen installation was carried out successfully"; "Glycol flow issues to the PCS Chiller … at 15:48 the Glycol supply dropped below 1.8 gpm"; PCS filter "might be clogged with debris which accumulated during this maintenance period." Weather fine (RH <20%, wind <4 m/s). Closure = camera/glycol recovery inside a maintenance period (partly planned).

"Both telescopes off-sky tonight. Simonyi is unable to move in Azimuth, the plan is to take calibration all night." "electronics team stablished we can not enable the TMA Azimuth drives with one missing encoder. Telescope will remain off-sky until Monday." Glycol PCS filter changed (flow 2.6 → 7.5 gpm at 14:12 UT). Calibrations from 00:46 UTC (tunable laser power issues, OBS-1230), PTC from 02:52 UTC. Weather clear.

"Both telescopes off-sky. Taking PTC calibration data all night." (TMA az encoder still out.) "BLOCK-T563 started at 22:29 and will run all night." Electrometer 103 faults (OBS-1020): 02:40 UTC "~80 minutes", 07:10 UTC "~10m", 09:20 UTC "call it a night … ~40 minutes" — calibration time only. Weather good (RH ~16%, wind <5 m/s).

"Simonyi and AuxTel were off-sky." "Simonyi TMA azimuth axis still awaiting alignment of one encoder head." "Ran the LSSTCam PTC curve until 09:00 UTC"; Electrometer 103 faulted four times (~15 min); "End of the night at 10:00 UTC." Weather clear, seeing ~1″.

"TMA encoder 1 is back and Simonyi onsky again with FBS all night." Initial alignment 23:28 UTC ("delayed by about 0.55h", OBS-1883 shutter telemetry); TMA Softmotion fault 23:40 UTC ("0.25h lost"); on-sky FBS 00:03 UTC; MTDome az fault 00:40 UTC ("0.37h time lost", OBS-646); "FBS LSST Survey ran for 8.2h without any fault"; scheduler stopped 10:15 UTC. ≈1.2 h lost to faults. Weather clear, RH <8%.

"Normal night split between FBS-driven AOS Stability tests and Pre-LSST, which ended dramatically with MTAircompressor fault resulting in Cascade of M1M3, MTMount, MTAOS, MTPtg faults. Systems were recovered at the cost of morning Calibration time." Alignment ~22:00 UTC; scheduler config issue "time loss ~0.5hr" (OBS-1847); pre-LSST from 23:32 UTC; "stopped at 09:23 UTC due to fault (~-17 sun El)"; dome closed 10:27 UTC. ≈1.5 h lost to faults (start + early stop). Weather dry, wind ~5 m/s.

"repeated MTMount faults and failure to home Az axis … resulting in a total of ~ 40 min observing time loss" (OBS-1886). AOS tests to ~03:00 UTC, "FBS survey started around 03:11 UTC and continued throughout the night". MTAirCompressors 1 and 2 faulted ~00:45 UTC. "We had begun observing through the clouds towards the end of observing night (hence the high PSF)." Wind ~12 m/s.

"Observatory state = DOWNTIME. Dynalene leak detected from the top-end assembly this morning … LOTO applied to TMA and Dome tonight. No Simonyi observing." "No night operations." Sky clear until ~03:00 UTC; AuxTel "Early shutdown due to" clouds (AuxTel statement).

"TEA leak is resolved. We're back in operation! But the sky was sad and cloudy so we spent time being operational under a closed dome." "Dome and louvers opened at 22:32 UTC. Dome closed at 23:17 UTC due to clouds." "Dome opened again at 00:32UTC. Dome closed at 01:23 UTC due to clouds"; "00:34 UTC T539 Initial Alignment: failed due to clouds rolling in." Monochromatic flats from 02:00 UTC, CBP sweeps 07:43 UTC. No on-sky data; laser tracker (OBS-1825) and louver compressor breakers affected calibrations only.

"In general was a good night of FBS, we just have 1h lost with MTMount + we turn on the camera heater tape." Dome opened 21:50 UTC; alignment 22:57 UTC; "FBS from 23:38 UTC on"; heater tape 04:00 UTC; MTMount fault 06:28 UTC (OBS-641). "Camera vacum was decreasing to fast, the recomendation of the camera team was finish the night and send TMA to horizont" (end time not given); M1M3 faulted going to horizon. Clear, cold (7 °C), dew point −5 °C.

"Smooth FBS night, some Mount errors that were addressed without major complication." Alignment 23:18 UTC; FBS 23:54 UTC; "At 09:58 UTC we got another MTMount fault, and due to time constraints we decided to close the dome at 10:11 UTC". 4× MTDome az error (OBS-646), MTMount faults (OBS-641, OBS-1113), 2× no-heartbeat script failures (OBS-1124). Clear, wind ~5 m/s, RH ~10%.

"On-sky most of the night. Frequent MTMount faults, improved by using CCW Drive 2. Frequent MTDome Errors." Dome opened 22:05 UTC; "22:44 - 23:30 UTC initial alignment, interrupted by MTMount fault followed by failing to home Az axis. 23:30 UTC: FBS resumed"; "lost ~12 minutes" homing (OBS-1897). Power: "There was a power outage during the dome handover (~19:55 UTC), all system recovered fine"; "Power cut at the end of the night - issues with both Dynalene and Glycol, the glycol chiller 2 is off … Camera remained out of danger zone." — power glitch ×2, flagged (no on-sky loss stated). Stable weather, wind <2 m/s; seeing worsened to ~1.5–3″.

"FBS only night, we finished the observations early due to weather conditions." "clear night up to 9:20 UTC, then very cloudy but low humidity <10%." Dome opened 22:08 UTC; alignment 22:59 UTC; "23:11 UTC FBS started"; "09:20 UTC we finish the observation due to weather conditions" (≈1 h lost vs ~10:30 UTC ends on nearby nights). 09:43 UTC both observers trapped in the elevator (OBS-1901, after observing). "Chiller 2 was recovered after the power glitch in the morning" (the 05-18 end-of-night cut).

"No on-sky observing with Simonyi or AuxTel due to poor weather conditions." "No on-sky observing due to poor weather conditions (~8hrs time loss)." "Closed-dome for the start of the night due to total cloud coverage." "Around 3:41 UTC, the weather looked optimistic, so we attempted to go on-sky. However, it turned out to be a 'sucker hole,' so we went back to calibrations." TunableLaser CSC faulted ~04:45 UTC (OBS-1905, calibrations only); "By 9:00 UTC we called the night early".

"Engineering tests at the beginning and pre-LSST for the rest of the night. M1M3 Fault due to disabled FA 428 which needs fixing - forced us to run FBS at 10% speed settings. Multiple MTDome Az Errors and MTMount faults due to CCW issues." Dome 22:07 UTC; alignment 22:36 UTC; engineering blocks 23:11–00:42 UTC (planned); "00:42 UTC - Pre-LSST survey." M1M3 fault cascade incl. Scheduler (OBS-1908); "Multiple interruptions due to MTMount and MTPtg Faulting" (OBS-1467); difficult homing (OBS-992). Clear, wind <5 m/s.

"Smooth on-sky operation but clouds come and go." "Cirrus clouds passed through at the beginning of the night"; "Partially cloudy during the night. wind ~ 10m/s". "BLOCK-624 FBS: smooth operation till 02:30 UTC. Only paused briefly to restart top end hex"; M1M3 bending test 02:30–03:30 UTC (planned); FBS 03:40 UTC to end of night. Dome az fault (OBS-646), top-end heat exchanger not responding, homing failed (OBS-1897). No loss quantified.

"Due to issues related to daytime troubleshooting … we were delayed from on-sky operations until 00:38 UTC (~2hrs observational time loss)" — daytime: MTCamera in fault, take_image failure (OBS-1909), "TMA main cabinet fault occurred (18:34 UTC) … RMCFaulty state (OBS-1217)". Alignment 00:43–00:52 UTC (redone, OBS-1249); "BLOCK-T624 … (00:58 - 9:46 UTC)"; softmotion faults "time loss 0.22hrs" (OBS-641). "Closed dome by 10:00 UTC due to poor weather" — wind ">10-15m/s" (≈0.5 h early). TMA at 10% settings (FA 428). ≈2.2 h fault + ≈0.5 h wind.

"We observed through most of the night, suffering some time loss due to MTDome issues and a few mount errors that we recovered from quickly." "time loss totaled less than 1 hour for the night" (OBS-641, dome script time-outs). Dome opened 22:23 UTC; alignment at −10°; "FBS Survey started at -12deg, some clouds interrupted the beginning of the night a bit" — "thin cirrus … cleared after midnight", wind 7–9 m/s, seeing >1″.

"Simonyi Pre-LSST Survey run the entire night." Alignment at sun el −10°, pre-LSST at −13°; "dome Az drivers went to fault several times (OBS-646, minimal time lost)"; fans off 09:47 UTC. End-of-night MTMount/M2 fault (OBS-1914) and LOVE MTQueue failure (OBS-1915) — "no cals were taken" (calibrations only). Wind 5–10 m/s, seeing 0.7–1.5″. AuxTel in scheduled shutdown (AuxTel statement).

"We ran FBS the entire night. Minimal fault loss due to some elevation and azimuth drive errors on the mount." "FBS started at 22:54 UTC"; "some (30 minutes) of fault loss to OBS-641". "instantaneous wind gusts reached up to 16 m/s, but were never sustained long enough to merit dome closure"; wind ~12 m/s, DIMM seeing up to 2″.

"Cloudy sky tonight so we focused on calibrations." "At sunset thick clouds appeared and covered the entire sky." "Cloudy night conditions prevented us from going on sky, so we switched to closed-dome tests." "We took calibrations the entire night." Wind ~10 m/s, RH 20%.

"Difficult night start although we made it for different initial alignment configurations. Nominal FBS observations, no issues." Daytime: "DPs were not retracted properly, preventing us from removing LPs for TMA. This was the main reason why we were delayed for starting the initial alignment (OBS-1921)." "Venting started at -3 deg sun elevation after we were able to solve the issue with TMA"; alignment "at 23:07 UT (Sun elevation -16.5 deg)"; mount soft-motion fault 23:18 UTC; alignment repeated 23:24 UTC; "different initial alignment MTAOS, rotator configurations until 00:40 UTC" (pointing-model investigations, partly deliberate); "FBS started at 00:47 UTC." ≈1.5 h late start vs 23:10 UTC starts on nearby nights — fault/engineering mix, ambiguous. Wind <10 m/s, RH ~20%.
"regular day with timely start of pre-LSST. very good night with pre-LSST." "FBS started at 23:10 UTC. FBS finish at 10:36 UTC." Seeing ~0.6″, RH ~7%.

"Good night of Pre-LSST, regular issues with the MTMount and MTDome." "Started the night with M1M3 Thermals way out of spec and losing TMA Az encoder heads" (two heads lost 19:00–20:00 UTC daytime; "Took about 14 tries to home the Az axis"). "We lost some time with MTMount Fault and finding a good Az away from W and the rising full moon … initial alignment at -15 Sun El ~ 23:00 UTC; repeated twice." "Pre-LSST started at 23:20 UTC. Pre-LSST ends at 10:35 UTC." Thin high clouds cleared early in the night.

"Pre-LSST FBS observations ran until clouds covered the sky forcing us close and we run Monochromatic Flats." "22:00 UTC --> Dome shutters + louvers opened"; "22:46 UTC --> Initial alignment"; "22:57 UTC --> Pre-LSST FBS Start"; "02:12 UTC --> Close Dome because weather (cloudy)"; calibrations from 02:50 UTC; minimal cals 10:40 UTC. ≈3.3 h on sky, ≈8 h lost to clouds; "Cloudy Night, wind ~ 15 m/s". "MTMount faults continued throughout the night" (OBS-1930).

Planned: "Simonyi is running RGA for the camera vacuum. Off sky for tonight." "Dome closed, no tests performed by OSs as TMA was locked at horizon. Mirror faulted due to a small earthquake, so it will remain lowered until we can move from horizon." Also ESS 404/405 faults, dome errors at handover (FRACAS-396). Weather would have been marginal anyway: "Overcast during the first few hours, then winds gust over 15 m/s" (AuxTel statement: closed until 09:00 UTC).

"Simonyi: No observations due to TMA faults." Initial alignment started 23:00 UTC, "delayed by multiple MTMount faults and not being able to Home until 00:00"; "When we finally completed the initial alignment and started the FBS the MTMount faulted again." "Persistent TMA faults prevented observations throughout the night … we decided to close the dome at 03:55 UTC." TMA parked at Az ≈ −2°, could not home azimuth. Weather fine: wind 5–10 m/s, RH 11–17%, clear start.

"We ran FBS survey from 00:42 - 6:36 UTC." "At 4:43 UTC, LSSTCam's focal-plane faulted … (OBS-953 0.4hrs time loss)." "By 6:36 UTC, clouds had worsened to the point where MTAOS was failing due to lack of wavefront data, so we closed and proceeded with in-dome calibrations (4hrs time loss)." In-dome CBP attempt failed (TunableLaser fault, OBS-1823); "ended the night early around 9:30 UTC". ≈ 4.4 h lost, mostly clouds. TMA fans vec-01/02 would not turn off (OBS-1936).

"Very productive night. Very few faults that took us off sky." T539 initial alignment 22:41–22:50 UTC, T668 closed-loop TARTS 22:58–01:00, "T624 FBS Survey: 01:00 to 9:00 UTC. Night finished early due to cloudy weather." "Around 9:00 UTC, clouds came in that were too thick to push through. We closed early." ≈ 1.7 h lost. One MTDome az drive error (OBS-646); CBP afterwards failed (tunable laser, OBS-1937).

"On-sky observations were not conducted due to cloud cover. Instead, closed-dome tests were performed." "Sky was cloudy throughout the night … average wind speed was around 14 m/s." CBP multiple pointings 23:42–06:48 UTC, then M1M3 thermalization test; "The sky cleared briefly around 08:00 UTC (for about 1-2hrs); however, an M1M3 thermalization test was already in progress, and the decision was made to continue the test." Tunable laser faulted twice, recovered; lighting-control delay (OBS-1938).

"Weather was started off cloudy tonight, but cleared up and we were able to observe with Simonyi and AuxTel the majority of the night." T668 at 22:46 UTC (unsuccessful), pre-LSST from 23:50 UTC. "Clouds were impacting observations periodically throughout the night. We waited in 30min intervals … Total time loss was ~0.75hrs." EGW pump turned off ~03:05 UTC (OBS-1942), "M1M3 thermal gradients were outside operational limits for most of the night"; MTAOS faulted multiple times from no wavefront data (OBS-1943). Dome closed ~10:38 UTC.

"Pretty calm and good weather so FBS ran quite smoothly for the entire of the night." Initial alignment 22:10 UT; "FBS observations started at 23:01 UT and finished at 10:38 UTC." MTAOS faults 00:44 and 04:24 UTC, "We lost a few mins." Power glitch (control room): "All the power of control room workstation were down from 02:40 CLT to 04:00 CLT. Systems were fine and we could monitor them with our personal laptops" (OBS-1944); BLOCK-T733 skipped because of it.

"The night was cloudy, so only closed-dome tests were performed." "Whole night was cloudy … average wind speed 11 m/s." CBP same-quadrant test ~23:00–06:41 UTC; LinearStage102 faulted ~07:30 UTC and could not be recovered (~1.5 h troubleshooting), "Therefore, we concluded the night" (OBS-1945). Tunable laser fault 02:30 UTC; ESS 404/405 faults. Daytime power glitch: "At 15:50:30 we had a power glitch. Twenty seconds later the generators started"; glycol chiller 2 went down 15:53, recovered 16:42 UTC.

"We spent the night in planned downtime due to clouds. We took in-dome calibrations." "Heavy clouds and strong winds, some snow flurries from the neighboring mountains, and a temperature of 3-5 degrees C." Also partly planned: "We decided in the morning to lock the telescope out at horizon to do helium sniffing overnight with the camera"; filter change during the day. Calibration start delayed by OSS fault found at handover, troubleshooting with electronics support (OBS-1946); frequent Tunable Laser faults (6–7).

"Today was weather downtime from later half of the daytime." "Cold day and night (~3.5 C) with moderate winds, and light snowfall in the morning. Clouds cleared up after midnight." "The summit facilities were evacuated after lunchtime, and nighttime observer support from the control room was canceled." Observers monitored the M1M3 FCU thermalization test remotely from the hotel all night.

"Night full of pre-LSST survey with few interruptions due to overcast, MTMount faults and difficulties homing." Dome opened 22:20 UTC; TMA homing from 23:05 UTC "took for ever, around 1.3h" (OBS-1987); initial alignment 00:39 UTC, FBS from 01:02 UTC (≈ 2.2 h late). "[02:57 UTC] MTMount fault due to multiple Encoder faults. Caused us over 1 hour of delay due to difficulties with homing." Ran at 5% speed settings from discovery at 05:33 UTC. "Clouds were coming and going all night." Road was closed earlier in the day (previous night's weather).

"Bad night with frequent MTMount faults; but we managed to get decent data." "First seven hours of the night were marred with frequent MTMount Faults, with cadence of 20 min and later few minutes. We had a total of 15 faults in this time." Recovery "within 10 min" each (≈ 2–2.5 h cumulative); fixed by a patch to MTMount CSC, "[07:09 UTC] we crossed the 20 min mark of continuous observations". On sky 23:40 UTC, pre-LSST 23:52–10:33 UTC. "We observed all night through 30% cloud cover." Dome handover delayed by blown fuses in the capacitor bank.

"Cloudy night, poor seeing. Closed 1 hour early due to clouds." "Pre-LSST FBS operations started at 23:11 UTC." "Multiple MTAOS faults starting at 07:30 UTC due to clouds. Closed dome 1 hour early due to frequent MTAOS faults." Heavy clouds, wind ~8 m/s. Minimal daily cal flats skipped (electrometer.103). Daytime: mild earthquake (5.0) faulted M1M3; power outage in the control room from a laptop charger on the workstation strip (OBS-1944, daytime, flagged).

"Observing through the clouds for the first half of the night and taking calibration data for the second half of the night." Initial alignment 22:35 UTC, "22:47 UTC Starting FBS observations"; "05:01 UTC Stopping the FBS and closing Simonyi due to severe overcast and worsening prediction until the morning." "Overcast of ~27% at the beginning of night, worsened to 38% at 04:57 UTC when we closed both telescopes." ≈ 5.7 h lost of ≈ 12. Then monochromatic/whitelight flats in-dome; laser-tracker alignment not possible (OBS-1530).

Mixed weather + planned: "Simonyi stayed at horizon with the pump cart connected. M1M3 thermal tests were done overnight." "A few stars poking through the clouds but too overcast to work." "The TMA was not handed over to the observers and remained parked at the horizon. The Camera Team (SM) and KN connected the pump cart in preparation for the sniffing test scheduled for tomorrow" (planned). Dome opened at 00:51 UTC only for BLOCK-T740 off-sky M1M3 fan-speed test. Pneumatic louver air leak noted (OBS-1967).

Mixed weather + planned: "Overcast, closed domes, TMA at horizon with LSSTCam connected to pump cart. M1M3 FCU tests only." BLOCK-T740 off-sky test 21:20 → 12:30 UTC. "The TMA was handed over to the observers but remained parked at the horizon. G6 decided to allow the camera team (SM) and KN to continue working on the camera for the sniffing test" (planned). Also "running on generator power until tomorrow", "MTMount is operating in CCW-only mode", "The pneumatic louvers are not operational". Wind 10 m/s, overcast.

"Simonyi was closed at 2:00 UTC due incoming weather affecting the road to the observatory." "Due to concerns about the road integrity, observatory personnel were told to leave the observatory by 2:00 UTC. After midnight, temperatures dropped to sub-freezing and humidity rose to 100%. Some light snowfall." Evening spent on TMA oil test (T734) and M1M3 fan test (T740); "Parked the telescope at horizon and left the observatory for the hotel". Dome locked out by engineering, no handover. Power glitch: "Around 20:12 UTC, we had multiple power glitches that powered off Chiller 2 on level 1"; "Additional power glitches before midnight" (OBS-1969); both air compressors shut off (OBS-1970). Camera He sniffing continued by day (leak still at FT24).

"Simonyi and AuxTel were kept off-sky due to poor weather conditions during the day and ice on both domes. Night was spent running calibration tests." Day: "fog, ice, rain, etc. Temperatures were between -1 and 1°C, and humidity was at 100%." "Day crew announced that we will remain off-sky for the night since they were not able to inspect dome conditions before leaving." Sky cleared by nightfall. Calibrations from ~23:00 UTC with repeated tunable laser faults (20–30 min recoveries), MTMount softmotion fault (OBS-641); TMA parked at horizon with platforms deployed for filter swap. Glycol chillers telemetry incident ~20:00 UTC (OBS-1971).

"Pretty calm and stable night. We ran two AOS tests, and pre LSST survey." Initial alignment 22:36 UTC; AOS blocks T736/T614; pre-LSST 01:01–01:47, T698 02:02–03:02, pre-LSST 03:05–10:23 UTC. "MTMount Axis FAULT at 01:03 UTC … Recovered in 6 mins" (OBS-959); MTAOS fault 04:05 UTC (OBS-1928). "after 2 a.m. CLT, we could see the sky covered by some clouds" → low image quality but observing continued. Observing without pneumatic louvers and with louver E1 closed (OBS-1974). Daytime filter swap u→y failed (loader liquid leak).

"Cloudy all night." "By the afternoon, the weather was not looking promising for observing, so we decided to set-up and run TCBP tests (BLOCK-T737, T738, T739)." TCBP tests all night; MTCamera HV trips at 04:25 UTC after an image with dome lights on (30 min), resumed 05:04 UTC. End of night: "several MTMount, MTRotator issues and the third one even having MTPtg fault" (OBS-1979); "At 10:54 UTC, we noticed we lost cry 4 … started to heat up the Cryo 4 on L7 from 11:27 UTC" — start of the camera cryo outage. Generator power during the day (substation maintenance).

"Daytime was dedicated to Cryo4 recovery and OSS troubleshooting. Nighttime observations with Simonyi telescope were therefore cancelled." "No observations during the night." OSS could not start in the morning (communication timeout, TMA internal error, 3-way valve stuck at 100%), returned to service after 3 h (OBS-1980). Pump cart connected; later a communication failure sent the camera to safe state. Weather clear and dry ("no clouds but seeing ~1.7").

"No Simonyi tonight." "a decision was made to warm up the LSSTCam in order to continue operations more stably. The whole night dedicated to the observations with AuxTel only." Cryo 4 nearly ready, Cryo 5 leak found with blockage, Cryo 6 controller swap pending; warm-up/N2 purge "could delay start-up until Wednesday or Thursday". Weather stable (RH 10%, wind ~5 m/s).

"Simonyi downtime continued as the telescope remained locked out for camera cryo repair." "Telescope locked at horizon." Cryo 4 purged, Cryo 5 leak repair not concluded, Cryo 6 controller swapped. Weather "Clear and chilly all day", seeing ~1.1″, minimal wind.

"Downtime continues for the Simonyi as the camera cryo investigations continue. Cool down was initiated tonight." "the leak [Cryo 5] is not reparable in the few days we might have. Cryo 6 was unclogged, cryo 4 exhibited symptoms of not being healthy." Weather clear, no clouds, minimal wind, seeing 1.1–1.13″.

"On Sky with LSSTCam again. Calm night." "We got on sky around 23:48 (about 1.2 hours delayed)" — delay from "an mysterious issue with cryo4 (flux inversion)"; then "the scheduler kept faulting due to a fixed az position … We had to reach out to science support to reconfigure the scheduler … Finally started directly with PreLSST." "Pre LSST from 1:36 UTC" (≈ 2.8 h late vs a normal ~22:50 UTC start). Then T698 stability tests (2 × 1 h) and pre-LSST to −12°. "No issues during the night." "We are running on about 3.5 cryo circuits and pushing it." Winds ~0–5 m/s, DIMM 0.7″.

"Excellent session for the FBS, ~11.5h with no faults on sky, stable seeing around 0.98\", and median PSF FWHM of 0.77." Initial alignment 22:40 UTC, "[23:01 UTC] - FBS started", "[10:43 UTC] - Observation finished at sun elevation -12°. ~11.5h on sky." MTDome GIS errors (OBS-1987) "No on-sky time lost"; script failure seq 45–56 (OBS-1986). RH < 12%, wind 3.5→6.5 m/s.

"Full night of FBS Survey with minimal issues (~11.5hrs of observation)." "23:00 FBS Survey started." "10:40 Stopped observations and closed dome." Poor seeing early (1.5″ PSF, DIMM 2″); "By the later half of the night, cloud coverage rolled in from the South, limiting observations to mostly the North. Clouds disappeared around 8:00 UTC" — no loss stated. Pre-sky OSS faults (chillers restart) and two MTMount faults, before 23:00.

"Another full night of FBS survey with minimal issues on Simonyi. Weather conditions were clear and dry." "23:20 Starting the FBS." "00:12 OSS faulted and MTMount faulted" (duration not given). "10:01 MTMount CSC faulted due to encoder head 1 being lost while tracking (OBS-1445). Back observing around 10:10." "10:40 Stopped FBS survey and closed dome." RH < 5%, wind < 5 m/s; clouds rolled in ~09:00 UTC.

"Simonyi completed its first (unofficial) night of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time! We took 875 science exposures." "Scheduler:1 resumed at 22:48 UTC when the Sun elevation was -11.8 deg, marking the official start of the LSST"; "continued for 12 hours with minimal interruptions"; "We stopped observations at 10:45 UTC". "At 1:30 UTC, MTScheduler faulted due to an unexpected TimeoutError" (OBS-1994). "Clouds rolled in around 4:00 UTC, but disappeared after a couple of hours." Elevation software-limit interlock engaged when parking (OBS-439).

"Day 2 of the LSST Survey is complete! We had a couple of TMA incidences that took significant time off-sky to recover. That--along with high wind gusts at the end of the night--resulted in an earlier shutdown … we managed to gather around 10hrs worth of observations." Survey from 22:49 UTC. "6:46 UTC MTMount elevation drives faulted due to a faulty Hall Sensor issue (OBS-1002) … Time loss was 0.75hr." "8:54 UTC There was another MTMount fault … Total recovery time was around 1.65hrs." "Around 9:45 UTC the wind gusts were extremely high: 15-20m/s"; "we decided to abandon the last 45min of the night"; "We closed dome at 10:15 UTC." ≈ 2.4 h fault + ≈ 0.75 h wind/OSS.
No night report found (database outage; tailgate: "Could not send the nightlog for the same reason", OBS-2000).
No night report found (same outage).

"Calibration night due to high wind." Nighttime "wind 15-20 m/s". Also "Main Cabinet special fault occurred four times at 21:02 UTC … attempts to power on OSS were unsuccessful"; PXI–Bosch PLC problem 23:43 UTC; "TMA is recovered at 02:15 UTC"; earthquake 03:10 UTC, recovered 04:45 UTC. Calibration blocks rest of night. Weather and faults overlap; wind was at the CLOSE threshold.

"Since it was not possible to recover the TMA, there were no night operations for Simonyi today. The main cabinet continued to fault" ("Cabinet Temperature decreased below critical limit", from 23:49 UTC). Weather: "gusts reaching 20 m/s … no Auxtel operations" (AuxTel statement).
"Flawless FBS night for Simonyi, only one MTAOS timeout that was quickly recovered." FBS from 00:27 UTC to 10:40 UTC. Seeing 2″ early ("summit heat bubble").
"On sky all night, some good seeing." TARTS test abandoned (RA config), FBS whole night. "Slight delay to get on sky as the camera got stuck integrating (guider error) … began alignment around -13".

"Observations with Simonyi were suspended to give time to thoroughly investigate the camera fault that occurred during the day" — "all but 4 of the 71 REBs of the camera powered off spontaneously" at 09:56 local. OSS faulted the mount at the cal screen (OBS-2006). Weather good (cirrus, 0.7″).

"Camera was recovered and ready to go on sky at 02:20 UTC"; "FBS started at 03:15 UTC"; HV bias tripped 03:30–03:50 UTC (OBS-2010); two MTAOS timeouts; done 10:40 UTC. Weather: "Mostly cloudy … became worse by 23UTC when we decided to close AuxTel and Simonyi … Around 23UTC, clouds cleared". ≈4 h lost at start, camera recovery dominant, clouds coincident.

"Delayed start on-sky due to cloud coverage. No faults from Simonyi the entire night!" Alignment waited until 23:00 UTC; survey 01:30–10:44 UTC; "Cloudy sky overall, but we were able to observe through them".

"Weather was very cloudy for most of the night"; alignment stopped 23:33 UTC "due to clouds faulting MTAOS"; in-dome CBP from 03:00 UTC; "Clouds cleared up around 5:20 UTC"; survey 06:10–10:45 UTC. ≈6 h lost to clouds; dome az drives errored on unpark (OBS-646), MTAOS fault from RA errors (OBS-1532).
"Nearly flawless night … We shutdown 1hr early due to one of the observers not feeling well." Survey 00:10–09:45 UTC; MTRotator fault 08:30 UTC (OBS-1481). 1 h lost to staffing, not weather/fault.

"Relatively smooth except for a glycol chiller 2 failure after power glitch" ("power glitch at 06:30 UTC, and glycol chiller 2 stopped (OBS-1214). Oscar remotely started it" — no observing loss stated). "Closed early at 4am due to backup shift drove to reach the summit" (≈3 h lost, staffing). FBS from 23:06 UTC. Power glitch flagged.
"Both Simonyi and Auxtel observed throughout the night without any issue. End of the night around 11:00 UTC." Seeing ~0.6″ at start.

"Calibration night with many tunable laser faults." "We attempted to run the initial alignment (thin clouds passing), but after one attempt … decided to proceed with the in-dome calibrations as the weather conditions deteriorated." "Cloudy whole night", wind ~12 m/s. (Report's "11:35 UTC" for the suspension is likely a typo for 23:35 UTC `[check]`.) Last night before the storm evacuation.
